issues.summary: MEDIUM: AgentConsole engine selector resolved the agent's granted engines with a prefix-only filter (e.server_id.startsWith('mind.')), so de-prefixed ClotoHub catalog engines (e.g. deepseek — bug-388/396 de-prefixing drops the legacy mind. namespace) were excluded from agentEngines. A deepseek engine granted to an agent therefore appeared as not connected in the chat console, even though AgentTerminal/AgentPluginWorkspace (which use isEngineServer) recognised it correctly. Same de-prefix holdout class also affected preset detection (presets.ts detectPreset counted a granted de-prefixed engine as a non-engine server, breaking active-preset match). Reported by user 2026-07-01.

Related same-class holdout NOT changed: AgentConsole.tsx thinking-viz event filter uses engine_id?.startsWith(mind.) — left as-is (broadening risks cross-agent event leakage; de-prefixed engine thinking events for THIS agent are still caught by the agent_id clause). Reverse-polarity: verifies the SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL grace path is present.

issues.fix_note: Fixed in 0.6.8 (PR #2 Group B1): build_and_register's common-module and target-server pip installs were converted from piped .output() to the null-stdio .status() / spawn_uv_streaming idioms used by the batch path (concurrent pipe drain + timeout), eliminating the back-pressure deadlock risk. Reverse-polarity: verifies presence of the bug-369 fix markers.

issues.summary: Setup wizard silently skips preset apply when API key is missing
Setup wizard has hardcoded English strings not covered by i18n
Installation proceeds even if preset apply fails — agent grants not configured
Corrupted venv directory not cleaned before re-creation attempt
Server marked installed even when registration succeeds but connection fails
GitHub unreachable during setup — no retry button shown to user
Unnecessary to_string_lossy() roundtrip when passing paths to Command::new() — use PathBuf directly
issues.fix_note: Re-triaged 2026-06-29 (wontfix): most to_string_lossy() calls in marketplace.rs are necessary because the spawn command is persisted as a String (MgpServerConfig.command / mcp_servers.command DB column), so PathBuf cannot replace them. issues.summary: Python Launcher (py) may not exist on Windows Store or conda Python installs
setup-complete.json deleted while DB exists triggers unnecessary re-setup
Setup status reports complete when mcp-servers directory is missing
Preset server IDs not validated against marketplace registry before install — addressed by bug-381 (backend notification)
Missing server in preset silently skipped during batch install — no user notification

Setup Wizard still bounces on first finish click and re-appears on next launch after fresh install — bug-383's `useRef(true)` consumed the gate at the post-onComplete transition, not at App mount; backend `setup_complete=false` on the Skip and SSE-failure paths compounds the issue across sessions
issues.fix_note: Three-prong bundle. (Prong 1, main.tsx) replace `useRef(true)` with `useRef<boolean>(setupDone)` so the version-upgrade re-check fires only when the session began with a stored completion flag — on a fresh install the gate starts `false` and the effect can never bounce the post-onComplete transition. (Prong 2b, SetupWizard.tsx) when the install-progress `EventSource` errors before a `Complete` payload, surface a retry-able error via the existing `installError` UI instead of auto-advancing the wizard to step 6 with no install artefacts. (Prong 2c, handlers/setup.rs) relax the bug-378 fallback to require only an `agents` row, so users who explicitly Skip the marketplace install are not re-prompted through the wizard on every launch — DEVELOPMENT.md §1.9 documents the new doctrine that `setup_complete` is the kernel's minimum-proof-of-boot contract, not a check on optional install artefacts. bug-383 remains marked `fixed` (its useRef-based gate was the right shape, just initialised wrong) and its `pattern` is updated to the corrected call form that ships with this PR.

issues.summary: Setup Wizard finish button bounces user back to step 0 — useEffect re-checks setup status immediately after onComplete and unmounts the wizard when backend reports incomplete
issues.fix_note: main.tsx had a useEffect that re-ran `api.getSetupStatus()` every time `setupDone` flipped. The intent was the version-upgrade scenario (stale `cloto-setup-completed=1` in localStorage from an older kernel), but the effect also fired immediately after `onComplete()`, which sets `setupDone` false→true. If the backend reported `setup_complete=false` at that moment for any reason (e.g. Setup Wizard skipped install via the step-4 Skip path, or a transient Windows path quirk), `setSetupDone(false)` was called, unmounting the wizard and remounting it at step 0 — making the wizard appear unfinishable. Gated the re-check behind a `useRef` initialised to `true` and consumed on first eligible run, so the version-upgrade flow still triggers on the App's first mount but the finish click is trusted as a terminal user action. Exposed on Windows NSIS install (bug-382 hotfix unmasked the wizard which was previously unreachable due to kernel boot failure). NOTE: superseded by bug-384 — the `useRef(true)` initialisation still consumed the gate on the first eligible run, which on a fresh install is the post-onComplete transition the fix was meant to skip; bug-384's `useRef<boolean>(setupDone)` captures the correct mount-time state. The `pattern` for this entry is updated to track the corrected call shape so the registry remains [VERIFIED] without changing the historical record of bug-383 itself.

issues.summary: CRITICAL: kernel fails to boot on Windows NSIS install with 'Cloto Kernel failed to start: アクセスが拒否されました。(os error 5)' — DATABASE_URL default + storage dirs land under Program Files
issues.fix_note: DATABASE_URL fallback (config.rs) and the storage directories created at boot (lib.rs L62 tracing, L384 attachments/avatars/vrm/speech) were hard-coded to `exe_dir()/data/`. NSIS places `cloto-system.exe` under `C:\Program Files\cloto-system\` which is not user-writable for standard accounts, so `create_dir_all` returned `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` and the FATAL `?` at lib.rs:370 crashed the kernel on first boot. Introduced `config::data_dir()` helper that takes a dev/prod split via `is_dev_layout()`: dev (Cargo.toml detected by walking up from current exe) keeps `<exe_dir>/data` to preserve `target/debug/data/cloto_memories.db`; production routes through `dirs::data_dir().join("cloto-system")` giving `%APPDATA%\Roaming\cloto-system\` on Windows, `~/Library/Application Support/cloto-system/` on macOS, `~/.local/share/cloto-system/` on Linux. handlers/agents.rs speech reader updated to match. MCP server bundle layout (mcp_venv.rs / managers/mcp.rs `<exe_dir>/data/mcp-servers/`) is a separate workflow tracked as follow-up.

issues.summary: CRITICAL: 'Failed to apply update' — applyUpdate spawns non-existent sidecar 'cloto_system' via @tauri-apps/plugin-shell, bypassing the configured Tauri Updater plugin
issues.fix_note: applyUpdate() shelled out to a sidecar binary `cloto_system` via @tauri-apps/plugin-shell, but the binary is never bundled into the NSIS / DMG / .deb installer — `bundle.externalBin` is unset in tauri.conf.json and the release.yml build-tauri jobs do not copy the standalone cloto_system bin into the app bundle. Every Update Now click failed at Command.create() with a 'program not found' style error, which the UI surfaced as the default 'Failed to apply update' message. Compounded by checkForUpdates() using GitHub API directly (rate-limited 60 req/h unauth) instead of the configured Tauri Updater endpoint. The Tauri Updater plugin itself was fully wired up (pubkey + endpoint=latest.json + createUpdaterArtifacts:'v1Compatible'), and CI generated a valid latest.json per release — the dashboard simply never invoked it. Switched applyUpdate() to @tauri-apps/plugin-updater check() + downloadAndInstall() and @tauri-apps/plugin-process relaunch(); unified checkForUpdates() to the same check() API to drop the GitHub API path; removed the now-dead shell:allow-execute cloto_system entry from capabilities/default.json. Affects all installer paths from 0.6.3 onward — existing 0.6.3 / 0.6.4 users must manually download 0.6.5 to recover the auto-update flow. Known limitation: latest.json resolves via GitHub `/releases/latest/download/` which only points to stable releases; pre-release channel discovery is deferred to a future feature.

issues.summary: CRITICAL: 'Failed to apply update' on 0.6.5 → 0.6.6 auto-update — productName change (cloto-system → ClotoCore) suspected to break NSIS in-place upgrade path even though identifier (com.cloto.app) is unchanged
issues.fix_note: Added a Tauri 2.x NSIS PREINSTALL hook at `dashboard/src-tauri/installer.nsh`, wired via `bundle.windows.nsis.installerHooks` in `tauri.conf.json`. The hook probes both `HKLM` and `HKCU` for `Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\cloto-system` (covering `installMode: "both"`), and when a legacy 0.6.5-era install is detected, silently invokes its `UninstallString` via `ExecWait '"$0" /S'`. The Tauri 2.x uninstaller's `un.SEC_APPDATA` section is not selected by default under silent mode, so user data at `%APPDATA%\Roaming\cloto-system\` survives the migration — `config.rs:37` continues to resolve `data_dir` to that literal path post-upgrade, preserving chat history, agent state, embedding namespaces, `mcp_access_control` grants, and registered MCP servers. The new 0.6.7 install proceeds to `{autopf}\ClotoCore\` via Tauri's default flow and registers a fresh `HKLM\…\Uninstall\ClotoCore` key. The hook is a no-op on fresh 0.6.7 installs (no legacy uninstall key present). Companion fixes shipped in 0.6.7: bug-387 (PR #152, dashboard env_var `name` field) and the release.yml two-phase upload race (PR #151). Sandbox verify pre-tag confirmed: legacy uninstaller ran, `%APPDATA%` data preserved, fresh `ClotoCore` folder created, new uninstall registry key at `HKLM\…\Uninstall\ClotoCore`.

issues.summary: CRITICAL: Marketplace install dialog reads env var keys from `ev.key` but the mgp-sdk wire serializes the field as `name` — all env_vars collapse to a single `{undefined: <last default>}` state slot, so the form shows every field with the same value, and the install request body sends a malformed `env: {undefined: <value>}` map that the backend rejects with `Failed to install marketplace server: Bad Request`. Blocks all marketplace installs of servers that declare any env_vars (CPersona, cmemo, cscheduler, etc.) on 0.6.6.
issues.fix_note: Latent regression introduced when mgp-sdk renamed `EnvVarDef.key` → `EnvVarDef.name` (with `#[serde(alias = "key")]` covering deserialize-side backward compatibility only; serialize always emits `name`). The Rust backend forwards the catalog response verbatim through the Tauri command, so the dashboard now receives entries shaped `{name, default, description}` from ClotoHub `/api/catalog`. The dashboard's `EnvVarDef` TypeScript interface (`dashboard/src/types.ts`) and `InstallDialog.tsx` were never updated and still read `.key`, which is `undefined` for every entry. The seven `.key` references in `InstallDialog.tsx` (state init for required + optional env_vars, the `isRequired` predicate, React list key, label text, controlled input value, and the onChange propagation) all collapse to the same `undefined` slot, causing every input to render the value of whichever env_var was processed last (in CPersona's case `CPERSONA_AUTO_CALIBRATE`'s default `"false"`). Submitting the form posts `{server_id, env: {"undefined": "false"}, auto_start: true}`, which the kernel's marketplace handler rejects with HTTP 400. Fix replaces `key` → `name` in `dashboard/src/types.ts:259` and the seven `ev.key` / `v.key` references in `InstallDialog.tsx`. This is the TypeScript-side counterpart to the `feedback_serde_alias_pub_use_field_rename` gotcha — the Rust alias only papered over the wire mismatch on the deserialize path, not the cross-language consumer's read path. The legacy `cloto-mcp-servers/registry.json` `key` shape is still accepted on ingest by mgp-sdk's alias, but is no longer emitted on any wire the dashboard consumes.

issues.summary: HIGH: Migration 20260524010000 (rename memory.cpersona -> cpersona) is not idempotent when BOTH the legacy `memory.cpersona` row AND a marketplace-installed `cpersona` row exist in mcp_servers: the rename UPDATE collides with the PRIMARY KEY (UNIQUE constraint failed: mcp_servers.name, code 1555) and the kernel aborts at boot (FATAL: Database migration failed). Affects any pre-0.6.6 user who installed cpersona from the catalog before first booting a >=0.6.6 build. Repro 2026-06-10 on dev target/debug/data (ledger stopped at 20260524000000). Manual repair: migrate mcp_access_control grants to 'cpersona', delete legacy row, reboot (migration then no-ops).
issues.fix_note: Fixed by repair_cpersona_rename_collision (db/mod.rs), which runs before sqlx migrations in init_db: when migration 20260524010000 has not been applied and both 'memory.cpersona' and 'cpersona' rows exist, legacy grants are merged onto 'cpersona' (explicit dedup; mcp_access_control has no UNIQUE constraint), plugin_configs duplicates are dropped (its (plugin_id, config_key) PK collides on the migration's UPDATE the same way), and the legacy mcp_servers row is deleted — the checksummed migration then no-ops. Covered by a test that replays the actual migration file after repair. NOTE: the buggy migration file itself is intentionally unchanged (sqlx checksum); this entry's check therefore verifies the presence of the repair guard rather than the absence of the original SQL.

issues.summary: HIGH: needs_common detection tests the legacy flat layout location (servers_dir/common/__init__.py) which marketplace git-clone installs never populate; any pre-existing legacy copy there (or its absence) makes the check meaningless for the nested clone layout (mcp-servers/<directory>/servers/common). A stale legacy common/ silently suppresses the shared-package provisioning for new installs (observed 2026-06-10: needs_common=false for all 4 connectors despite manifest dependencies=["common"]).
issues.fix_note: Fixed: needs_common no longer probes the legacy flat layout. All three call sites (monorepo tarball, git install, setup-wizard batch) now derive needs_common from the declared dependency alone; provisioning happens via uv pip install into the shared venv (resolve_common_source picks the nested-clone sibling or flat copy).

issues.summary: HIGH: the needs_common rescue (uv pip install of the shared 'common' package into the venv) is dead code — it requires servers_dir/common/pyproject.toml, but cloto-mcp-servers' servers/common ships as a plain package directory with no pyproject.toml (verified in working tree and tag v0.1.5/v0.1.7). Even with needs_common=true the install is silently skipped, so manifest install.dependencies=["common"] is never honored; connectors without a self sys.path bootstrap die with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'common' (cscheduler, 2026-06-10, fixed server-side in cloto-mcp-servers#28). Fix options: ship a pyproject.toml in servers/common, or provision via PYTHONPATH/.pth instead of pip.
issues.fix_note: Fixed two-sided: clotohub-servers v0.1.8 ships servers/common/pyproject.toml (setuptools package-dir mapping exposing the 'common' import package), and ClotoCore's rescue uses resolve_common_source to probe the nested git-clone sibling (<clone>/servers/common) before the legacy flat location, warning loudly instead of silently skipping when no installable tree is found.

issues.summary: CRITICAL: Magic Seal verification hashes config.command instead of the actual entry-point script. For every interpreter-launched server (command="python", script in args[0]) Path::new("python").exists() is false, so verification is skipped via the entry_point_not_a_file branch and the server is force-downgraded to Untrusted — the catalog-issued seal (which binds the server.py bytes) is never checked against anything. Observed 2026-06-10: all 4 marketplace installs (cscheduler/deepseek/terminal/websearch) logged TRUST_LEVEL_DOWNGRADED_NO_SEAL reason=entry_point_not_a_file despite valid hub seals. The seal chain is effectively disabled for all Python marketplace servers; fix should resolve the sealable file as the script path (args[0]) when command is an interpreter.
issues.fix_note: Fixed by resolve_sealable_entry_point (managers/mcp.rs): when command is an interpreter (python*/node/deno/bun), the sealable file is the first non-flag arg (the entry-point script the catalog seal binds); binary servers keep command. Bare 'python' marketplace installs now verify the hub seal against server.py instead of skipping via entry_point_not_a_file; an absolute venv interpreter can no longer mismatch a script-bound seal.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: marketplace uninstall file cleanup resolves the on-disk directory via the catalog cache (effective_install_dir) and falls back to server_id as the directory name. When the server has no current catalog entry AND its install directory differs from its id (e.g. legacy registry installs: id mind.deepseek, dir deepseek), the fallback path does not exist and remove_dir_all is silently skipped, orphaning the installed files. Observed 2026-06-10 uninstalling mind.deepseek/tool.terminal/tool.websearch — DB rows removed, flat dirs left behind.
issues.fix_note: Fixed: uninstall now probes candidates in order — catalog effective_install_dir, the directory derived from the registered entry-point args (install_dir_from_args reads mcp_servers.args BEFORE remove_server deletes the row), then server_id — removes the first that exists, and warns instead of silently no-oping when none is found.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: dashboard fetchJson/mutate discard the kernel's JSON error body and surface only res.statusText, so a 400 ValidationError like "Server 'cpersona' is already installed" reaches the user as just 'Bad Request'. This masked the real rejection reason behind the long-standing «CPersona raw_url install 'Bad Request'» mystery (an earlier decision narrative) — the synchronous install_handler validations are the only Bad Request sources; the raw_url path itself reports errors via SSE StepError and was never reached. A throwIfNotOk helper with body-message extraction already existed in api.ts but neither generic path used it.
issues.fix_note: Fixed: fetchJson and mutate now route !res.ok through the existing throwIfNotOk helper, which extracts body.error.message (kernel AppError shape {error:{type,message}}) and falls back to statusText only for non-JSON bodies.

issues.summary: HIGH: marketplace installs store the catalog seal (HMAC-SHA256 of the hub's canonical message, signed with the HUB master key) into mcp_servers.seal, but spawn-time verification computes HMAC(local kernel seal.key, entry-point FILE BYTES) — two different protocols that can never match. Any fresh kernel that marketplace-installs a sealed catalog connector hard-blocks at spawn with 'Magic Seal verification failed — binary may be tampered' (SealStatus::Failed). Existing installs carry the same stored seal and hit the identical block on their next restart. Surfaced by the an earlier decision Step 4 fresh-kernel E2E (cscheduler via blob-mirrored raw_url; extraction and common provisioning succeeded — the block is purely the seal check). Proper fix is the deferred post-MVP roadmap item 6 (Ed25519 public-key verification of the hub canonical message via /api/seal/keys + plain entry_point_sha256 integrity compare); interim options are catalog-side entry_point_sha256 keyless integrity verify or not passing the hub seal into the local HMAC verifier.
issues.fix_note: PROPER FIX landed (an earlier decision, roadmap item 6) on top of the interim (b'): the catalog serves the seal's dual-signature record (RegistryEntry.signature_payload, mgp-sdk v0.5.0, clotohub-web PR #30); local_seal_for_install verifies the Ed25519 signature over mgp_seal::canonical_message(id, version, entry_point_sha256) against the hub JWKS (/api/seal/keys, in-memory 1h-TTL cache + kid-miss refetch) and mints a LOCAL seal only on signature + hash match (declared tier preserved). D2 bifurcation: unsigned / JWKS-unavailable / malformed register unsealed (spawn forces untrusted per §10 inv 3); signature_invalid / integrity_mismatch hard-block as tamper suspects. Trust anchor upgraded from 'HTTPS to the catalog' to 'the hub's Ed25519 key'. The remaining `seal: entry.seal.clone()` occurrence is the display-only catalog UI projection. Interim history: keyless hash check + local re-seal (mgp-sdk v0.4.0, clotohub-web PR #29, ClotoCore PR #176).

issues.summary: HIGH: sandbox_base_dir (and therefore the Magic Seal key directory, sandbox_base_dir.parent()/seal.key) defaulted to the CWD-relative "data/mcp-sandbox" instead of being anchored to the absolute data_dir(). data_dir() resolves to exe_dir()/data (e.g. target/debug/data) where the install-time seal.key lives and every server seal is minted, but the relative default resolves against the process CWD. Launching the kernel from a different CWD (notably `tauri dev`, CWD = dashboard/src-tauri) makes load_or_generate_seal_key read dashboard/src-tauri/data/seal.key — a DIFFERENT key — so check_seal recomputes a non-matching HMAC and every sealed MCP server (cpersona, deepseek, cscheduler, terminal, websearch) hard-blocks at spawn with 'Magic Seal verification failed — binary may be tampered'. This is NOT bug-394 (the stored seals are valid local HMACs for the real data dir; only the key path is wrong). Proven: cpersona's stored seal HMAC-matches ONLY target/debug/data/seal.key (not dashboard/src-tauri/data/seal.key), and the running kernel (CWD=dashboard/src-tauri, no CLOTO_SANDBOX_DIR/CLOTO_SEAL_KEY set) created dashboard/src-tauri/data/mcp-sandbox.
issues.fix_note: Fixed: the default sandbox_base_dir now resolves to data_dir().join("mcp-sandbox") (absolute, exe-anchored) so sandbox_base_dir.parent() == data_dir() and the seal.key path is CWD-independent. The CLOTO_SANDBOX_DIR override path is unchanged. After the fix the kernel reads the correct target/debug/data/seal.key and sealed servers whose entry-point files are intact verify. Separate, still-open issue (not this entry): cscheduler/deepseek carry doubled install paths (mcp-servers/servers/<id>/servers/<id>/server.py) pointing at wrong/stub files, which fail seal under any key — to be tracked on its own.

issues.summary: HIGH: Agent.default_engine_id 'mind.deepseek' is unresolvable — the agentic loop resolves an engine by EXACT server-name match (run_agentic_loop: `if mcp.has_server(engine_id).await`, system.rs ~1369, with no 'mind.' prefix/alias normalization), but the DeepSeek connector installs under the ClotoHub catalog id 'deepseek' (the catalog renamed the connector mind.deepseek -> deepseek), so its registered MCP server name is 'deepseek'. has_server("mind.deepseek") is false and no Rust plugin matches, so every think / think_with_tools for an agent whose default_engine_id is 'mind.deepseek' (agent.cloto_default, agent.karin, agent.cpersona_bench) returns the literal string "[Error] Engine 'mind.deepseek' not found" as the response content. mind.local works only because its server name literally is 'mind.local'. Runtime-proven 2026-06-14: with the deepseek MCP server Connected (2 tools, seal verified) the Phase 5 A/B probe got the not-found error for all 14 queries until agent.cpersona_bench was repointed to default_engine_id='deepseek'. This silently corrupted the first A/B pass (the error string contains no contaminant keyword, so the heuristic classifier scored all turns 'coherent' = a false 0% drift). NOTE: the real evidence is runtime (the error string + the agents / mcp_servers DB rows); the pattern below only pins the exact-match resolution locus, so this stays expected=present until a fix changes that line.
issues.fix_note: run_agentic_loop engine resolver now tries exact MCP server match first, then falls back to the `mind.`-stripped id (e.g. mind.deepseek -> deepseek) and rebinds engine_id to the actual server name so every downstream call_kind_at/has_kind_at targets the right server. This binds connectors that the ClotoHub catalog renamed by dropping the `mind.` namespace prefix. Pattern repointed to the fallback check (has_server(stripped)) as a regression guard: its absence now signals the alias fallback was removed.

issues.summary: HIGH: GET /api/mcp/servers/:name/settings returns 500 'Internal Server Error' for every MCP server. db::get_mcp_server_settings's SELECT omitted the `seal` column (added by migration 20260508000000_add_mcp_server_seal) while McpServerRecord declares `seal: Option<String>`, so sqlx FromRow fails with ColumnNotFound and the handler maps it to AppError::Internal (HTTP 500). The sibling query load_active_mcp_servers selects seal correctly — this query was missed when the column was introduced, so the server-list and config panel render (list endpoint) while the settings tab shows 'Failed to get server settings: Internal Server Error'. Surfaced 2026-06-29 on cpersona (running, 27 tools) but affects all servers regardless of seal value.
issues.fix_note: Added `seal` to the get_mcp_server_settings SELECT column list to match McpServerRecord and the sibling load_active_mcp_servers query. Guarded by the db::mcp::tests::get_mcp_server_settings_selects_seal_column regression test (covers seal=Some and seal=NULL decode); the pattern pins that test name.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: interpreter-launched MCP servers were spawned without verifying the entry-point script exists, so a stale/missing entry-point failed opaquely. When a server's recorded args path goes stale (observed on cscheduler/terminal/websearch, whose rows carried a doubled install path mcp-servers/servers/<name>/servers/<name>/server.py from a past server-side catalog directory bug, with the files no longer on disk), the kernel ran `python <missing>/server.py`; python exits immediately and the failure surfaced only as 'error, 0 tools' in the dashboard with no indication of the cause. Robustness fix for an earlier decision; the root install-path doubling was a clotohub-servers catalog issue (directory field = 'servers/<name>') since corrected to flat names.
issues.fix_note: Added validate_entry_point_exists() called in StdioTransport::start before spawn: resolves the entry-point via resolve_sealable_entry_point and, only for absolute paths, bails with 'entry-point not found — reinstall this server from the marketplace' when it is missing. Skips `python -m module` (bare module name) and relative scripts (cwd-dependent) to avoid false negatives; also covers missing Rust binaries. Guarded by 4 unit tests (managers::mcp_transport::tests::entry_point_*).

issues.summary: HIGH: marketplace install writes a DOUBLED on-disk path for monorepo connectors, so the server fails to launch. effective_install_dir returned the catalog `directory` verbatim, and the install/extract/register/uninstall sites join it with the source `subdir`. When the (hub-served) catalog `directory` carries the monorepo-relative path 'servers/<name>' AND `subdir` is the same 'servers/<name>', target_dir = mcp-servers/servers/<name> and server_path = target_dir/servers/<name> → entry-point mcp-servers/servers/<name>/servers/<name>/server.py, which does not exist → 'error, 0 tools'. Reproduced after a reinstall on 2026-06-29 (cscheduler/terminal/deepseek error; websearch only worked because its files happened to land at the doubled path). The local cloto-mcp-servers/registry.json already has the flat directory ('websearch' etc.), so the deployed hub catalog is stale — but the kernel should not double regardless. Continuation of an earlier decision / bug-398 (which only clarified the resulting error).
issues.fix_note: effective_install_dir now collapses a multi-segment value to its final path component (trim slashes + rsplit on '/'\\'), so a malformed catalog directory='servers/<name>' becomes the flat install dir '<name>'; target_dir/subdir then stays single-nested (mcp-servers/<name>/servers/<name>/server.py, matching a nested git clone). Well-formed flat directories and dotted ids (memory.cpersona) are unchanged; all three lock-step sites (extract/register/uninstall) use this fn so they stay consistent. Upstream follow-up: republish the hub catalog from the corrected registry.json. Guarded by effective_install_dir_collapses_monorepo_relative_directory.

issues.summary: CRITICAL: marketplace uninstall is vulnerable to path traversal → arbitrary directory deletion. DELETE /api/marketplace/servers/:id takes `server_id` from the request path unvalidated and pushes it as a deletion candidate joined onto servers_root (data_dir/mcp-servers), then tokio::fs::remove_dir_all. `DELETE /api/marketplace/servers/%2e%2e` makes servers_root.join('..') resolve to data_dir itself → recursive wipe of cloto_memories.db, mcp_access_control grants, embedding namespaces, cron jobs and audit logs (the exact irreplaceable state the Destructive-DB rule protects). The sibling create_mcp_server runs validate_server_name (rejects '..','/'); uninstall_handler did not. Authenticated (check_auth) but any granted client can trigger it.
issues.fix_note: uninstall_handler now (1) rejects any server_id containing '/', '\\' or '..' up front with AppError::Validation, and (2) backstops every deletion candidate (catalog/args/id) with a canonicalized containment check — the resolved target must start_with the canonicalized servers_root and must not be servers_root itself — before remove_dir_all. Catalog/args candidates were already collapsed to a single path component; the raw server_id fallback was the live traversal vector. Marker: the 'path traversal blocked' warn message.

issues.summary: HIGH: UTF-8 char-boundary panic in the MCP stdio response loop. On an unparseable line, mcp_client.rs logged `&line[..line.len().min(200)]` — a byte slice. When a multibyte codepoint straddles byte 200 (e.g. a long non-JSON diagnostic/traceback printed to stdout by a Python server), the slice panics, aborting the spawned response-loop task. After that no responses are delivered for that server: pending oneshots time out and every tools/call hangs until request_timeout_secs, and is_alive()'s channel-based liveness keeps the health monitor from restarting it — a permanent wedge until kernel restart.
issues.fix_note: Replaced the byte slice with char-safe truncation `line.chars().take(200).collect::<String>()` so a multibyte boundary can no longer panic the response loop.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: UTF-8 char-boundary panic in cloto_shared::llm::parse_chat_think_result error paths. Both the invalid-JSON branch and the missing-choices[0] branch formatted `&response_body[..response_body.len().min(500)]` (byte slice). A provider error body >500 bytes whose multibyte codepoint (Japanese/emoji — common in this deployment) straddles byte 500 panics the think/parse call instead of returning the intended diagnostic Err.
issues.fix_note: Both sites now use char-safe truncation `response_body.chars().take(500).collect::<String>()`. Guarded by two regression tests (llm::tests::parse_invalid_json_with_multibyte_body_does_not_panic and parse_missing_choices_with_multibyte_body_does_not_panic) that place a 3-byte char across byte 500; the pattern pins the first test name.

issues.summary: HIGH: SSRF restricted-address check misses IPv6 link-local and IPv4-mapped addresses. SafeHttpClient::is_restricted_addr's V6 arm only blocked loopback, unspecified, fc00::/7 ULA and multicast. It did NOT block fe80::/10 link-local, nor IPv4-mapped addresses (::ffff:127.0.0.1, ::ffff:169.254.169.254) — Ipv6Addr::is_loopback() is false for mapped forms, so a whitelisted host resolving to ::ffff:169.254.169.254 reaches the cloud metadata endpoint even though the V4 path blocks 169.254.0.0/16. Gated by the host whitelist, but the comment claims DNS-rebinding/SSRF protection.
issues.fix_note: The V6 arm now (1) recurses into the V4 rules for v6.to_ipv4_mapped() addresses, and (2) adds fe80::/10 link-local ((seg0 & 0xffc0) == 0xfe80). Guarded by regression tests test_is_restricted_addr_ipv6_link_local and test_is_restricted_addr_ipv6_mapped_ipv4 (::ffff:127.0.0.1 / ::ffff:169.254.169.254 / ::ffff:10.0.0.1 blocked, ::ffff:8.8.8.8 allowed). Note: the DNS-rebinding TOCTOU (validated IP discarded, reqwest re-resolves the hostname) is tracked separately and still open.

issues.summary: HIGH (installed builds only): the MCP venv resolver anchors to exe_dir()/data instead of config::data_dir(), so installed builds can't find the marketplace-created venv. resolve_servers_dir_from_config and resolve_venv_dir probed exe_dir().join('data').join('mcp-servers'){/.venv}, but in a shipped build data_dir() is the platform user-data dir (dirs::data_dir()/cloto-system) — where the marketplace installs servers and creates the shared venv — while exe_dir()/data is the read-only app bundle. resolve_venv_python() therefore returned None and resolve_python_command fell back to bare python/python3 without the installed deps → every marketplace-installed Python MCP server crashes on import. Dev layout is unaffected (data_dir()==exe_dir()/data), so it never surfaced in `tauri dev`.
issues.fix_note: resolve_servers_dir_from_config and resolve_venv_dir now use crate::config::data_dir().join('mcp-servers'){/.venv} — the same anchor the marketplace and ensure_mcp_venv write to. In dev layout the two paths are byte-identical so dev is unchanged; only installed builds are fixed. Verified by absence of the old exe_dir().join("data") form in the file. Note: not runtime-verifiable in dev (prod-only path); change is behavior-preserving in dev.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: cron interval has no upper bound → i64 overflow → runaway perpetual dispatch. scheduler::calculate_initial_next_run validated an interval job's value only as parse::<u64>() and >= 60 (no max); calculate_next_run used .unwrap_or(3600). A large value (e.g. 99999999999999999, submittable via the cron API) makes interval_secs.cast_signed() * 1000 overflow i64 — in release it wraps to a past/negative next_run_at, so get_due_cron_jobs returns the job every tick and each dispatch kicks off a full agentic loop (LLM calls): a self-inflicted availability/cost DoS.
issues.fix_note: Added MAX_INTERVAL_SECS (1 year) + MIN_INTERVAL_SECS consts. calculate_initial_next_run now rejects intervals > MAX_INTERVAL_SECS; calculate_next_run clamps the parsed value to [MIN,MAX] and both use saturating_add/saturating_mul so next_run_at can never wrap into the past. Guarded by 4 tests (managers::scheduler::tests::initial_interval_* and recurring_interval_clamps_oversized_value).

issues.summary: MEDIUM: agent_id spoofing on the tool_hint direct-execution path. The main agentic loop force-overwrites identity (obj.insert('agent_id', agent.id)), but the tool_hint bypass path (used by I/O bridges, e.g. Discord backtick commands) used args_map.entry('agent_id').or_insert(agent.id), which KEEPS a caller-supplied agent_id. A bridge message whose tool_args already contains 'agent_id':'agent.victim' executes the tool (e.g. CPersona store/recall, or any granted tool) under the victim agent's identity, defeating per-agent access scoping.
issues.fix_note: The tool_hint path now force-overwrites agent_id with args_map.insert('agent_id', json!(agent.id)) — matching the main loop's anti-spoofing — instead of entry().or_insert(). A bridge-supplied agent_id can no longer survive.

issues.summary: HIGH: SSRF DNS-rebinding TOCTOU — the validated IP is discarded. capabilities.rs SafeHttpClient::send_http_request resolves the host, rejects restricted IPs, then throws the validated address away (`let _ip = target_ip...`) and issues the request against the original hostname (self.client.request(method, url)). reqwest performs its OWN second DNS resolution at connect time, so a whitelisted host whose DNS flips between a public IP (passes the check) and 127.0.0.1 / 169.254.169.254 (used for the actual connection) defeats the guard — the exact attack the 'DNS Rebinding対策' comment claims to prevent. Gated by the host whitelist (attacker needs a whitelisted domain they control).
issues.fix_note: Closes SAME-HOST connect-time rebind only. send_http_request no longer discards the validated address: it collects all resolved SocketAddrs, rejects the request if ANY is restricted, then builds a per-request reqwest client pinned to exactly that validated set via ClientBuilder::resolve_to_addrs(host, &resolved), so reqwest cannot re-resolve the ORIGINAL hostname to an unvalidated IP at connect time. SNI/Host keep using the hostname; multi-IP/HTTPS hosts do not regress; the long-lived reqwest::Client field was removed. NOTE: this does NOT close the redirect vector — a whitelisted host can 302 to a different host/IP that is re-resolved without the guard; that is tracked and fixed separately as bug-414 (redirects disabled). Guarded by capabilities::tests::test_send_http_request_blocks_whitelisted_host_resolving_to_loopback and test_send_http_request_rejects_non_whitelisted_host. Pairs with bug-403 (IPv6 restricted-addr gaps) and bug-414 (redirect bypass).
issues.notes: Fix: pin the connection to the validated IP — build a per-request reqwest client with .resolve(host, validated_socketaddr) (preserves Host/SNI), or connect to https://<ip>:<port> with an explicit Host header. Needs care to avoid TLS/SNI regressions on legitimate multi-IP HTTPS hosts; deferred from the 2026-06-29 audit batch for that reason. Pairs with bug-403 (IPv6 restricted-addr gaps, fixed).

issues.summary: HIGH: SSRF via redirect bypasses the SafeHttpClient whitelist + IP pin. capabilities.rs SafeHttpClient::send_http_request whitelists the host, resolves it, rejects restricted IPs, and (bug-407) pins the per-request reqwest client to the validated addresses — but reqwest follows up to 10 redirects by default and resolve_to_addrs only overrides DNS for the ORIGINAL hostname. A whitelisted host the attacker controls can answer `302 Location: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` (or any internal host/IP); reqwest follows it WITHOUT re-entering send_http_request, so the redirect target skips the whitelist check, skips is_restricted_addr, and has no IP pin — full SSRF to cloud-metadata / loopback in one hop. Pre-existing in the old shared-client design too; surfaced while reviewing the bug-407 fix.
issues.fix_note: The per-request client is built with .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none()), so reqwest no longer transparently follows 3xx responses to an unvalidated host/IP; a redirect is returned to the caller as-is. Capability HTTP probes do not need transparent redirect-following. This closes the one-hop SSRF that the bug-407 pin (same-host only) left open. Pairs with bug-407 (same-host connect-time rebind).
issues.notes: Alternative considered: a custom redirect::Policy that re-validates each hop's host against the whitelist and re-resolves+checks its IPs; rejected as more code for no benefit since capability probes don't need redirects.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: consensus aggregation race — a straggler proposal is mistaken for the synthesizer's output. consensus.rs: once proposals.len() >= min_proposals the session flips to Synthesizing and a synthesis request is dispatched, but from then the FIRST ThoughtResponse to arrive for that trace_id — from ANY agent — is taken as the synthesized answer (Action::Complete) and the session is removed. With min_proposals=2 and 3+ engines, a slow third engine's raw proposal that lands before the synthesizer's reply is returned to the user as 'consensus', and the real synthesizer reply then finds no session and is silently dropped.
issues.notes: FIXED (2026-06-30, an earlier decision): eliminated by the in-kernel consensus redesign rather than guarded. The event-driven ConsensusOrchestrator.on_thought_response (whose 'Synthesis complete via' branch accepted the first arriving ThoughtResponse for the trace_id as the synthesis — the race) was removed entirely; consensus.rs is now config + prompt helpers only. Consensus is orchestrated synchronously in SystemHandler::run_consensus: it collects all proposals, then runs the synthesizer in-kernel and stamps the synthetic agent id on the single terminal ThoughtResponse. Because collection and synthesis are sequential awaits in one task — not events matched by arrival order — a late proposal can never be mistaken for the synthesis result, and the out-of-repo agent_id-echo contract the reverted guard (481279c) needed is gone. Per-phase timeouts give the fail-safe (never a hung session). See docs/CONSENSUS_REVIVAL_DESIGN.md. HISTORY: an earlier standalone guard (commit 481279c, matching agent_id == 'agent.synthesizer') was reverted because it depended on the external MGP/SSE mind-bridge echoing AgentMetadata.id verbatim, which is unverifiable in-repo.

issues.summary: MEDIUM (HIGH if streaming exposed to untrusted servers): unbounded loop + allocation in StreamAssembler::record_chunk on an attacker-controlled chunk index. mcp_streaming.rs: a streaming MCP server sending one chunk with a large `index` (u32, up to 0xFFFFFFFF) while expected_index is small makes the gap-fill loop `for i in tracker.expected_index..index` iterate up to ~4.2 billion times, pushing each into tracker.gaps and gap_indices (~16 GB) WHILE holding the trackers mutex → hang/OOM blocking all stream tracking. Secondary: `tracker.expected_index = index + 1` overflows when index == u32::MAX (panic in debug, wrap in release).
issues.fix_note: record_chunk now caps the forward gap at MAX_STREAM_GAP (1024): a larger jump is logged and dropped (return None) instead of materializing up to ~4.2B entries under the trackers mutex, and all expected_index/received_count increments use saturating_add so index==u32::MAX no longer overflows. Guarded by managers::mcp_streaming::tests::assembler_caps_implausible_gap and assembler_max_index_no_overflow.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: unbounded read buffer in parse_sse_stream. mcp_transport.rs accumulates bytes into `buffer` and only drains on a newline. A remote/localhost MCP server that streams a large text/event-stream body WITHOUT any newline makes buffer grow without limit → memory exhaustion. (Secondary, perf-only: `buffer = buffer[newline_pos+1..].to_vec()` reallocates per line, O(n^2).)
issues.fix_note: parse_sse_stream now bounds the unterminated remainder at MAX_SSE_LINE_BYTES (1 MiB) and aborts the stream past it, so a newline-less body can't exhaust memory. Also replaced the per-line `buffer = buffer[pos+1..].to_vec()` (O(n^2)) with a single drain(..consumed) per chunk, and scoped the line borrow so it is released before the await.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: McpClient::is_alive() can't detect an idle child that has died → the health monitor never auto-restarts it. mcp_client.rs infers liveness from `!self.sender.is_closed()`, which reflects the writer task's receiver lifetime, not the child process or the read/response path. When a stdio server dies while idle, stdout EOF ends the response loop but nothing flips status to Error or closes the request channel, so the writer stays parked holding the Receiver, is_closed() stays false, is_alive() returns true, and the monitor (mcp_health.rs) never restarts it. It only self-heals after the NEXT tool call fails — i.e. after one user-visible failure + a full request_timeout_secs hang. Compounds bug-401's wedge.
issues.fix_note: McpClient now holds an alive: Arc<AtomicBool> (init true). The response loop clones it and stores false once the loop exits — which only happens on transport EOF (child gone), so an idle death is observed immediately. is_alive() reads `self.alive.load(SeqCst) && !self.sender.is_closed()` (both lock-free, no transport Mutex contention), so the health monitor (mcp_health.rs) restarts a dead-but-idle server without waiting for the next tool call to hang. The old 'Uses sender channel state' doc-comment (the bug anchor) is gone. Guarded by managers::mcp_client::tests::is_alive_flips_false_when_server_exits_idle (a mock MCP server answers initialize then exits → EOF). Compounded bug-401's wedge.
issues.notes: Fix: track real liveness — have the response loop set an Arc<AtomicBool> false on EOF/termination (it already detects this) and have is_alive() read that flag; or have the manager set status=Error when the response task ends. Don't rely on the writer task's receiver.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: audit-log writer uses a DEFERRED transaction (read-then-write) → un-retried SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT under concurrency. db/audit.rs write_audit_log_inner does pool.begin() (BEGIN DEFERRED) → SELECT chain_hash (read snapshot) → INSERT (upgrade read→write). Concurrent background audit writers (spawn_audit_log) both snapshot the same tail; the second's read→write upgrade returns SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT, which busy_timeout does NOT retry (snapshot conflict, not lock-wait). This is the mechanism behind the documented 'audit silent for 14h' incident; the retry ladder masks most but sustained concurrency permanently drops rows.
issues.fix_note: write_audit_log_inner now opens the transaction with pool.begin_with("BEGIN IMMEDIATE") (write lock taken at transaction start) instead of pool.begin() (BEGIN DEFERRED). Concurrent audit writers therefore serialize on the write lock — waiting out busy_timeout — instead of both taking a read snapshot and having the second fail its read->write upgrade with the un-retried SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT. begin_with returns a sqlx Transaction (RAII rollback on drop/cancel — see bug-415). Pattern anchor is the BEGIN IMMEDIATE string. Guarded by db::audit::tests::concurrent_audit_writes_all_persist (24 concurrent writers against a WAL file db, all rows must persist).
issues.notes: Fix: acquire the write lock up front — BEGIN IMMEDIATE for this tx (sqlx 0.8 custom begin), or serialize audit writes through a single-connection writer.

issues.summary: CRITICAL: audit write cancellation poisons the pool — regression introduced by the bug-412 fix (commit 95397e1, on branch fix/tier2-bug-backlog-137, not merged). The bug-412 fix replaced pool.begin() with a manual pool.acquire() + raw sqlx::query("BEGIN IMMEDIATE") + match { Ok => COMMIT, Err => ROLLBACK }, dropping sqlx's Transaction RAII rollback guard. write_audit_log wraps write_audit_log_inner in tokio::time::timeout (default 10s); if it cancels AFTER BEGIN IMMEDIATE but before COMMIT, the future is dropped and the PoolConnection returns to the pool with an OPEN write transaction — sqlx 0.8's SQLite pool release only pings, it does not roll back. The connection holds the WAL write lock; every subsequent audit writer blocks → SQLITE_BUSY → the retry ladder exhausts → permanent audit blackout until max_lifetime (~30min) recycles the connection. Strictly worse than bug-412 (the very 'audit silent' class it was meant to cure). The COMMIT-error path had the same defect (returned Err without rolling back).
issues.fix_note: Replaced the manual acquire + raw BEGIN IMMEDIATE + match(COMMIT/ROLLBACK) with `let mut tx = pool.begin_with("BEGIN IMMEDIATE").await?;` … SELECT/INSERT on &mut *tx … `tx.commit().await?;`. begin_with (sqlx 0.8 Pool::begin_with) still takes the write lock up front (satisfying bug-412) but returns a sqlx Transaction whose Drop queues a ROLLBACK, so a cancelled or COMMIT-failed write returns the connection to the pool clean — no dangling write lock, no blackout. Guarded by db::audit::tests::dropped_audit_tx_rolls_back_and_frees_pool (deterministically open BEGIN IMMEDIATE, write, drop uncommitted more times than the pool has connections, then assert a normal write still succeeds and only the committed row persists) and concurrent_audit_writes_all_persist (now on a WAL + 10s busy_timeout pool mirroring lib.rs). Regression introduced by the bug-412 fix; cross-ref bug-412.
issues.notes: Caught pre-merge by the post-fix adversarial review (2026-06-30). The earlier bug-412 test ran in DELETE-journal mode (sqlx 0.8 does not default to WAL) so it neither reproduced bug-412 nor caught this regression; the test pool now forces WAL + busy_timeout.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: Memory dashboard (MemoryCore) under-displays an agent's memories. The /memories and /episodes endpoints fetched a GLOBAL most-recent top-N (agent_id='' , limit 100/50) and the UI filtered by agent client-side, so any agent whose memories are not among the N most recent across ALL agents shows an incomplete or empty set. Observed: agent.karin had 9 memories in the DB but only its 2 most-recent rows were shown because 133 newer memories from other agents pushed the rest out of the top-100 window; the empty episode stream had the same cause.
issues.notes: Fixed by per-agent scoping. Backend: get_memories/get_episodes read an agent_id query param and pass it to list_memories/list_episodes (empty = global 'All' view). Frontend: api.getMemories/getEpisodes take an agentId and append ?agent_id=; MemoryCore.fetchData scopes the fetch to selectedAgent and re-fetches on change, and agentTabs is derived from the global getAgents() list (unioned with agent_ids in the data) so scoping no longer collapses the filter tabs.

issues.summary: LOW: MemoryCore renders an un-scopable empty-string ('') agent tab — narrow recurrence of bug-413. agentTabs unions agent ids found in the data, so a global-pool memory/episode carrying agent_id='' adds an empty-label tab. The backend cannot distinguish agent_id='' from 'all agents' (get_memories maps both an absent and an empty agent_id param to the global most-recent view), so selecting the '' tab fetches the unscoped global top-N and then client-filters to agent_id='' — for '' rows outside the top-100/50 window that is exactly the bug-413 under-display, reappearing for the global-pool bucket. Frontend-only; discovered by the post-bug-413 adversarial review.
issues.fix_note: agentTabs now removes the empty-string id (ids.delete('')), so no '' tab is offered; global-pool ('') rows are shown under 'All' (which maps to agent_id='' at the backend anyway). fetchData also treats both null and '' as the unscoped view (scope = selectedAgent || undefined), so a concrete agent id is the only thing that scopes the fetch. Cross-ref bug-413.
issues.notes: The backend can't separate '' from 'all' without an API change; excluding the '' tab is the minimal correct fix since '' rows are already visible under 'All'. A backend distinction (e.g. a sentinel for global-pool-only) was considered out of scope for a LOW edge.

issues.summary: HIGH: Consensus terminal response is never delivered to the originating chat — silent hang. SystemHandler::run_consensus produces the synthesized (or fail-safe error) text and calls emit_consensus_response, which ONLY sends a ThoughtResponse event stamped agent_id=consensus_config.synthetic_agent_id ('system.consensus') and never calls save_chat_message_reliable. The normal agentic path (system.rs ~1119-1137) persists the agent response under agent_id=agent.id with parent_id/branch threading before emitting; the consensus path has no persistence at all. Consequence: a 'consensus:'-prefixed message to agent.cloto_default leaves the user's chat with the user message and no response (GET /api/chat/agent.cloto_default/messages returns only the user turn; /api/chat/system.consensus/messages is empty), so the dashboard sits on thinking forever. This holds for BOTH the happy path AND every fail-safe branch ('[Consensus unavailable]', '[Consensus failed] N/min proposals', synthesis timeout), so the design guarantee in section 5.2 'the user never waits on a silent timeout' is violated — it merely becomes a silent error. Unit/integration tests only assert the ThoughtResponse event is emitted, never end-to-end chat visibility, so they pass while consensus is unusable in the chat UI. Live-reproduced 2026-06-30 (trace f98b7db4) on dev kernel :8081.
issues.fix_note: run_consensus now delivers the terminal answer (and every fail-safe error) via deliver_consensus_result: it persists the response under the ORIGINATING agent.id with save_chat_message_reliable (mirroring the normal path's parent_id/branch_index threading) and emits the ThoughtResponse stamped agent_id=agent.id (engine_id='consensus', metadata.consensus=true) — so it lands in the chat where the user asked and survives reload. The old emit_consensus_response (which stamped synthetic_agent_id and never persisted) is removed; the synthetic id is retained only as a metadata label, so the 'synthetic_agent_id.clone()' stamping pattern is gone. Per-step ConsensusProgress events feed the new dashboard Consensus tab. Covered by consensus_test.rs (terminal response under originating id + chat persistence + ConsensusProgress + MGP error code). bug-408 stays fixed (in-kernel synchronous orchestration stamps deterministically regardless of the chosen agent_id).
issues.notes: Carried in by the consensus revival (PR #230, an earlier decision); root-caused via live verification (trace f98b7db4). The synthetic_agent_id ('system.consensus') is now a display label in chat metadata, not the routing key. Cross-ref docs/CONSENSUS_REVIVAL_DESIGN.md sections 5.1/5.2.

issues.summary: LOW: The shipped CONSENSUS_ENGINES example references an engine that is not auto-registered, so consensus fails out of the box. installer.rs writes a commented '# CONSENSUS_ENGINES=deepseek,cerebras' example (de-prefixed from 'mind.deepseek,mind.cerebras' by an earlier decision; the pattern was updated to match, NOT because the bug was fixed), but only providers wired as a runtime engine server resolve in run_agentic_loop (engine_resolver: get_engine OR mcp.has_server(id) OR has_server(strip 'mind.')). On the dev kernel only 'deepseek' (an active agent's default engine) and 'mind.local' are registered engine servers; 'cerebras' exists in the llm_providers table but is not registered, so 'mind.cerebras' resolves to Err('Engine not found'), the engine is dropped, and a 2-engine config collects only 1 of min 2 proposals → quorum fail. The example thus produces a guaranteed failure for a user who copies it. Live-reproduced 2026-06-30 (trace f98b7db4: deepseek ok, mind.cerebras 'not found').
issues.fix_note: Fixed at the docs/config layer (an earlier decision), after the runtime premise was already reshaped by the bug-419 fix (engines are now sourced from the agent's granted engine servers, CONSENSUS_ENGINES is only a filter that never adds engines) and softened by the #232 engine-reuse quorum fallback plus the bug-417 fix (the '[Consensus unavailable/failed]' message is now delivered to the user's chat instead of being invisible). The installer template no longer ships the copy-paste example 'CONSENSUS_ENGINES=deepseek,cerebras'; it now documents the per-agent grant requirement (assign >= CONSENSUS_MIN_PROPOSALS engine servers to the agent in the Dashboard) and defaults the variable to empty. README gains a Consensus-mode section + corrected env table (default was wrongly listed as 'mind.deepseek,mind.cerebras'; CONSENSUS_PREFIX / CONSENSUS_AGENT_ID / CONSENSUS_ENGINE_REUSE rows added), ARCHITECTURE.md documents the in-kernel consensus flow.
issues.notes: Was: the shipped example referenced an engine that is not auto-registered, producing a guaranteed quorum fail for a user who copied it. Belonged to an earlier decision (config defaults/docs/marketing). Original fix options (a) reliable example ids / (b) document registration requirement / (c) boot warning — resolved via (b) plus removing the trap example; (c) is subsumed by the per-engine ConsensusProgress error events (MGP section-14 codes) on the dashboard Consensus tab.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: Consensus ran the global CONSENSUS_ENGINES list on every agent, ignoring per-agent engine configuration, so it executed engines the requesting agent was never assigned. SystemHandler::run_consensus took `let engines = &self.consensus_engines;` directly — a kernel-wide Vec<String> from the CONSENSUS_ENGINES env (config.rs) wired once in lib.rs — and ran each via run_agentic_loop under the originating agent, with engine resolution only checking global registration (get_engine / mcp.has_server), never whether the engine is one of the agent's granted engine servers. An agent assigned engines A+B would still have unrelated global engine C run under its identity, and the #232 engine-reuse fallback could mask a misconfigured/unregistered global engine. Decoupled from the dashboard's per-agent engine model (SetupWizard always grants the chosen engine; AgentConsole lists an agent's engines as its granted engine servers).
issues.fix_note: run_consensus now sources engines from the agent's own granted engine servers via agent_engine_servers() (filtering get_granted_server_ids by is_engine_server — mind.* prefix OR get_engine OR think/think_with_tools tool surface, matching dashboard serverCategory.ts isEngineServer / #234). The global CONSENSUS_ENGINES is demoted to an optional filter (filter_consensus_engines): empty = use all of the agent's engines, non-empty = intersect (mind. prefix normalized), never adding an engine the agent is not assigned. The direct `let engines = &self.consensus_engines;` is removed. Covered by consensus_engine_filter_tests (unit: empty passthrough / intersection / mind-prefix normalization / no-overlap) and consensus_ignores_global_engines_not_granted_to_agent (integration regression: a global list with engines the agent is not granted runs nothing).
issues.notes: User-reported 2026-06-30 ('consensus supports engines not configured on the agent'). Fix direction ratified by user: engines sourced from agent grants, CONSENSUS_ENGINES as filter (empty = all agent engines). Behavior note: with CONSENSUS_ENGINES empty, an agent granted >= min_proposals engine servers can now activate consensus on the 'consensus:' prefix (the prior additive-default G6 'empty = off' is intentionally relaxed). Cross-ref bug-417 (delivery) / bug-418 (unregistered-engine example) / docs/CONSENSUS_REVIVAL_DESIGN.md.

issues.summary: HIGH: The tool_hint direct-execution path bypassed per-agent MCP access control — an agent could invoke a tool on any connected server, including ones it was never granted. An external I/O bridge (e.g. a Discord backtick command) supplies metadata.tool_hint; SystemHandler::handle_message ran it via mcp.execute_tool_internal(tool_name, args) WITHOUT a check_tool_access / resolve_tool_access gate. execute_tool_internal resolves the tool through the GLOBAL tool_index, so any connected server's tool is reachable by name regardless of the requesting agent's mcp_access_control grants. The agentic loop gates tool calls (tool_names membership + execute_tool_for_agent -> check_tool_access), but the tool_hint bypass did not — so an agent could use an ungranted MCP server via a bridge-supplied tool_hint.
issues.fix_note: Originally fixed (PR #237) with a tool_hint-local bolt-on mcp.check_tool_access(&agent.id, &tool_name) before execute_tool_internal. That bolt-on is now REMOVED and SUBSUMED by the single capability gate (bug-421): the tool_hint path calls mcp.execute_tool_internal(&Caller::Agent(agent.id), ..), and the central gate (enforce_caller_grant, PATH 2) refuses any non-Allow before execution — identically to the agentic loop, which also routes through the same gate. Anchored on the 'bug-420' marker comment in the tool_hint block. Covered by tests/tool_hint_access_test.rs (ungranted/unavailable tool_hint refused before execution).
issues.notes: User-reported 2026-06-30 ('an agent can use an MCP server it is not registered/granted for'); confirmed path = tool_hint direct execution. Related: bug-419 (consensus engines), bug-173/174 (kernel-side tool validation / anti-spoofing). Follow-up (separate, not time-based): the mgp.agent.ask delegation loop (run_mgp_agent_ask_loop, mcp_kernel_tool.rs ~1824) executes engine tool calls via call_server_tool without a per-agent check_tool_access — tracked for a future hardening pass. | 2026-07-01: bolt-on superseded by the unified capability gate (bug-421).

issues.summary: HIGH: Per-agent MCP access enforcement was fragmented and non-deterministic, and reasoning ENGINES were never access-checked. Engine think/think_with_tools resolved globally (get_engine / has_server / call_kind_at) with no grant check, so an agent with ZERO grants still ran its engine and responded (LM Studio repro). The agentic-loop empty-grant branch fell back to the ungated registry.execute_tool, delegation (run_mgp_agent_ask_loop) executed engine/tool calls via call_server_tool with no per-agent check, and tool_hint used a separate bolt-on. The permission DATA model (mcp_access_control + resolve_tool_access) was already unified, but enforcement was scattered across call sites with inconsistent logic. Compounded by default_policy=opt-out (allow-all from migration 20260301), which also made revoking a grant ineffective (revoke-staleness).
issues.fix_note: Single capability gate threaded as Caller{Agent(id)|System} (no Default impl, so a missed site fails to compile) into BOTH manager-level execution chokepoints: PATH 1 = resolve_tool_call_target (call_server_tool/_streaming), PATH 2 = execute_tool_internal (the agentic loop + tool_hint path, which does NOT go through call_server_tool). enforce_caller_grant() consults resolve_tool_access(id, server_id, tool) once — covering engines (mind.* and bare-named MCP servers), tools, and memory uniformly. Kernel-native tools (mgp.*/gui.*) use enforce_kernel_rbac(): Deny-only on EXPLICIT deny entries via resolve_explicit_permission (default Allow), so the opt-in flip does not deny-by-default kernel tools. System callers (synthesizer via agent_type=='system', /api/mcp/call, switch_model, kernel cleanup, media preprocessing) bypass. The agentic-loop two-branch is collapsed onto execute_tool_for_agent (the empty-grant ungated branch is gone); execute_tool_for_agent's inline check_tool_access and the tool_hint bolt-on are removed (subsumed). Ships with migration 20260701000000: global opt-in flip + FK-safe non-clobbering engine backfill (default_engine_id -> server_grant). Anchored on the 'bug-421' markers in mcp.rs. Covered by db/mcp.rs resolve_tool_access unit tests, tests/engine_access_gate_test.rs (zero-grant agent denied engine; granted -> passes gate), and tests/tool_hint_access_test.rs.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: drain_all's global timeout cancels join_all, dropping in-flight drain futures between SIGTERM and SIGKILL, so a server that survives SIGTERM can leak past app exit. The Tauri app-exit drain (2000ms grace, 6s cap) is structurally guaranteed to hit the cap whenever any server needs escalation: drain_server worst case = 2s drain wait + 3s SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECS + 5s post-SIGKILL wait = 10s > 6s. On timeout the un-finished futures are dropped at their next await; one dropped after its SIGTERM but before the SIGKILL escalation leaves that child alive, and the app exit that follows runs no destructors (app.exit/process::exit), so kill_on_drop / transport Drop never fire. Observed 2026-07-11 (an earlier decision verification): every safe-shutdown run logged 'MCP drain_all timed out after 6s - 18 server(s) may not have shut down cleanly' (ERROR). In practice Python servers still exit on stdin EOF when the kernel dies, masking the leak; a server that ignores stdin EOF (Rust mgp-discord) would survive.
issues.notes: an earlier decision (an earlier decision). Fix directions: (a) make the per-server kill non-cancellable - spawn each drain as a detached task and have the timeout bound only the *wait*, never the kill; (b) scale the global cap to the per-server worst case (2s + 3s + 5s) instead of a flat 6s, and unify with the kernel endpoint's 5000ms/10s constants; (c) after a timeout, run a forced synchronous group-kill sweep over the still-registered children and log the sweep result (demoting the ERROR to WARN when the sweep confirms reap). Found while verifying the an earlier decision two-path safe shutdown; distinct from the mgp-discord mid-session restart leak (bug-427).
issues.fix_note: drain_all now runs each per-server drain as a detached tokio task, so the global timeout only stops waiting for them and can no longer cancel a drain between its SIGTERM and its SIGKILL escalation. Child pgids are snapshotted lock-free before draining (new McpClient::child_pid, captured at spawn — the response loop holding the transport Mutex cannot block it); on timeout a signal-only forced sweep SIGKILLs every recorded process group (ESRCH no-op for servers that already exited), so no child of a registered server survives drain_all returning, even when the caller exits without running destructors. The timeout log is demoted to WARN and reports the sweep result; non-Unix keeps the ERROR (subtree containment there needs a Job Object, tracked in an earlier decision). Regression test drain_all_timeout_sweep_kills_sigterm_immune_server: a SIGTERM-ignoring mock server against a 1s cap is dead after drain_all returns.

issues.summary: LOW: Rate-limit middleware returns a bare StatusCode, bypassing the JSON error envelope — rate_limit_middleware short-circuits straight to `StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` instead of an `AppError`/`ok_data`-style JSON body. ARCH §0.6 requires every REST response to go through the response helper so success and error bodies share one envelope; this is the one place in the HTTP layer that emits a bare status code with no body, silently breaking that contract specifically on the rate-limiting path (which is wired ahead of the router, so it applies to every route including ones that are otherwise fully AppError-consistent).
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2: 26 subsystem+security finders -> dedup -> severity-tiered adversarial verify; final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): http-handlers). Failure scenario: Any client that exceeds the per-IP token bucket (e.g. an aggressive frontend polling loop, a reconnect storm on the SSE endpoint, or a scanner) hits rate_limit_middleware's early return. Because the handler's return type is `Result<Response, StatusCode>`, axum resolves the `Err` branch via the blanket `impl IntoResponse for StatusCode`, producing an HTTP 429 with an EMPTY body and no Content-Type header — not the `{"error":{"type":...,"message":...}}` shape every other error path in the app produces via `AppError::into_response`. A frontend that does `const { error } = await res.json()` on any non-2xx response (the pattern implied by the uniform envelope) will throw a JSON-parse error on this specific status code instead of surfacing a normal error message. Fix direction: Change the middleware's error type from `StatusCode` to `AppError` (or build the same `{"error":{...}}` JSON body inline) so a 429 response carries the same envelope as every other error, e.g. return an `AppError` variant that maps to 429 with a `RateLimited` type/message.

issues.summary: LOW: Revoked API-key check silently skipped when the revoked_keys lock is contended — `check_auth_with_query` is synchronous, so it cannot `.await` the `revoked_keys` RwLock and instead uses `try_read()`. On the (rare but real) contention with the two writer paths — `invalidate_api_key` and the periodic DB-driven cleanup task — a lock-acquisition failure is treated as "skip the check" rather than "deny", making the revocation control fail-open instead of fail-closed for whatever request happens to race the write.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2: 26 subsystem+security finders -> dedup -> severity-tiered adversarial verify; final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): http-handlers). Failure scenario: A client presents an API key that was just revoked via `POST /api/system/invalidate-key`, or that the 6-hourly `cleanup_revoked_keys` sweep (lib.rs) is pruning at that moment. If that client's request happens to land in the brief window where the `revoked_keys` RwLock is held for writing (either write site), `check_auth_with_query`'s `state.revoked_keys.try_read()` returns `Err`; the code logs a warning ("skipping revocation check") and continues without ever consulting the revocation set, so the request is authenticated as if the key were never revoked. Fix direction: Make the auth check path async so it can `.read().await` the lock without racing, or switch `revoked_keys` to a lock-free structure (e.g. `ArcSwap<HashSet<String>>`) so reads never contend with the infrequent writes; in either case, treat an unresolvable check as deny rather than skip.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: import_memories writes its JSONL payload to a PID-only temp path, racing concurrent imports — The temp file used to hand JSONL data to the CPersona `import_memories` MCP tool is named only from the OS process id, so it is identical across every request served by this process. Concurrent imports collide on the same path with no locking or uniqueness, letting one request's write silently clobber another's data in the window between the synchronous `std::fs::write` and the async MCP call that consumes it, and letting one request's cleanup delete a file a concurrent request still needs.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2: 26 subsystem+security finders -> dedup -> severity-tiered adversarial verify; final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): http-handlers). Failure scenario: Two `POST /api/memories/import` requests land close together in the same kernel process (a double-submitted dashboard import, or an admin script firing several imports back-to-back). Both compute the identical path `std::env::temp_dir()/cloto-import-<pid>.jsonl` — `std::process::id()` is constant for the process's whole lifetime, not per-request. Request A's `std::fs::write` lands first, then A awaits the (non-instant, IPC-based) MCP `import_memories` tool call; before that call actually reads the file, request B's `std::fs::write` overwrites the same path with its own JSONL. The MCP server can end up importing B's data under A's `target_agent_id` while A's intended data is lost, and A's post-call `std::fs::remove_file` (line 658) can delete the file out from under a still-in-flight B. Fix direction: Generate a unique path per request (e.g. append a UUID or per-request counter to the PID-based name, or use `tempfile::NamedTempFile` which guarantees a unique path and cleans itself up), so concurrent imports in the same process never share a filesystem path.

issues.summary: CRITICAL: Marketplace `install_from_git` derives the clone/delete target from an unsanitized hub-served `id`/`directory`, allowing a malicious catalog entry to `remove_dir_all` outside `mcp-servers/` — install_from_git computes its clone/target directory as `servers_dir.join(effective_install_dir(entry))` and then deletes whatever is at that path with `remove_dir_all` before cloning, with no containment/canonicalization check against `servers_dir`. `effective_install_dir` (marketplace.rs:2500-2518) only collapses multi-component paths via `rsplit(['/','\\'])`; a single-component value of exactly `".."` (valid for both `entry.id` and `entry.directory`, neither of which is format-validated anywhere in `RegistryEntry` or the install path) is returned unchanged, so `servers_dir.join("..")` escapes to the parent (`data_dir`) directory. The exact same threat model — "the catalog `directory` is hub-served (and the deployed catalog can be stale/malicious)" — was already identified and fixed for `uninstall_handler` via a canonicalized containment check (bug-400, lines 607-704 of this file), but that fix was never applied to the install-side directory derivation, leaving `install_from_git` and the sibling `install_from_raw_url` (line 2101) exploitable via a normal marketplace-install click on a poisoned/compromised catalog entry.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2: 26 subsystem+security finders -> dedup -> severity-tiered adversarial verify; final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): sec-ssrf-path, marketplace). Failure scenario: A registry entry served by the (network-fetched, `hub.cloto.dev`-sourced or `CLOTO_CATALOG_URL`-overridden) catalog with `install.source.kind="git"` and `id=".."` (or `directory=".."`) with `directory` otherwise empty. `effective_install_dir` only strips everything up to the last '/'/'\\' via `rsplit`, so a bare `".."` with no separator passes through unchanged. `clone_dir = servers_dir.join("..")` resolves (via normal OS path resolution) to `state.data_dir` itself. Line 1874-1881 then unconditionally calls `tokio::fs::remove_dir_all(&clone_dir)` on that resolved path *before* the `git clone` even runs, recursively deleting the entire ClotoCore data directory (SQLite DB, access grants, embeddings, cron jobs, audit logs, secrets) the moment an authenticated user installs the poisoned entry. Fix direction: Apply the same defense-in-depth used in `uninstall_handler`: after computing `clone_dir`/`target_dir`, canonicalize `servers_dir` and require the (canonicalized, or joined-and-lexically-normalized like `validate_dest_path`) target to `starts_with(servers_dir)` and be `!= servers_dir`, refusing the install with a clear error otherwise. Alternatively/also, validate `entry.id` and `entry.directory` against the documented connector-id charset (`[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9_-]*[a-z0-9])?`) at the point the catalog is parsed/cached, rejecting entries that contain `.` `/` `\\` outside that charset before they ever reach `effective_install_dir`. — FIXED 2026-07-13 (branch fix/audit-critical-high): vulnerable anchor removed; verify-issues [FIXED].

issues.summary: HIGH: install_from_raw_url fetches an attacker/catalog-controlled URL with a bare reqwest client, bypassing the codebase's SafeHttpClient private-IP/localhost SSRF guard — Elsewhere in the codebase (capabilities.rs SafeHttpClient, used by managers/plugin.rs) outbound HTTP explicitly resolves DNS and blocks private/loopback/link-local/documentation/broadcast IPv4 and IPv6-mapped equivalents before connecting (ARCH §2.3 invariant). install_from_raw_url instead builds a bare reqwest::Client and fetches spec.url — a field that originates from the same hub-served/possibly-malicious catalog JSON the uninstall path explicitly distrusts (bug-400 comment) — with none of those protections, and without even calling the SDK's own RawUrlSpec::check().
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2: 26 subsystem+security finders -> dedup -> severity-tiered adversarial verify; final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): marketplace). Failure scenario: A catalog entry with install.source.type="raw_url" carries spec.url as free-form data (mgp_sdk::adapters::RawUrlSpec::check(), which only validates the scheme is http/https and that sha256 is 64 hex chars, is never even called in install_from_raw_url). A malicious/compromised catalog entry can set url to e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/..., or http://127.0.0.1:<internal-port>/..., or any internal-network address; install_from_raw_url builds `reqwest::Client::builder()...build()` directly and calls `.get(&spec.url)` with no host/IP validation. The response body is streamed straight to disk under state.data_dir/tmp/<id>-raw-url.tar.gz regardless of whether the sha256 check (which is itself optional per-entry) passes, giving an SSRF fetch-and-persist primitive against the host's internal network reachable from the normal single-server install flow. Fix direction: Route the raw_url download through SafeHttpClient (or equivalent private-IP/loopback resolution+blocking) before issuing the GET, and call spec.check() up front so at least the scheme is validated; consider also enforcing an allow-list of trusted download hosts for raw_url installs the way DockerSpec::check() is already invoked for docker installs. — FIXED 2026-07-13 (branch fix/audit-critical-high): vulnerable anchor removed; verify-issues [FIXED].

issues.summary: CRITICAL: Marketplace `install_from_raw_url` has the same unguarded `effective_install_dir` target, letting a malicious catalog entry wipe and then repopulate the app data directory via tar extraction — Identical root cause to the `install_from_git` finding, in the `raw_url` install path: `target_dir = servers_dir.join(effective_install_dir(entry))` is used directly for `remove_dir_all` + `create_dir_all` + tar extraction with no containment check against `servers_dir`/`data_dir`, even though the surrounding tar-entry extraction functions were hardened against zip-slip (`validate_dest_path`) and the sibling uninstall path was hardened against exactly this class of hub-served-path attack (bug-400). Because `effective_install_dir` does not reject a bare `".."` id/directory (no separator to strip on), the containment gap is fully reachable.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2: 26 subsystem+security finders -> dedup -> severity-tiered adversarial verify; final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): sec-ssrf-path, marketplace). Failure scenario: Same as the `install_from_git` finding but for `install.source.kind="raw_url"` entries: with `entry.id=".."` (or `directory=".."`), `target_dir` resolves to `state.data_dir`. Lines 2102-2109 do `if target_dir.exists() { remove_dir_all(&target_dir) }` then `create_dir_all(&target_dir)`, wiping the data directory; the subsequent `tar::Archive` extraction (`extract_tarball_stripped`/`extract_subdir_selective`) then writes the attacker-controlled tarball's contents directly into `data_dir` (each individual entry is still checked by `validate_dest_path` against `target_dir`, but `target_dir` itself is already the escaped, attacker-chosen directory, so that check provides no protection here) — giving the attacker both wholesale data loss and arbitrary file planting (e.g. overwriting `config.toml`, seeding a file an auto-started server will read) in one install click. Fix direction: Same as the `install_from_git` finding: add a canonicalized `starts_with(servers_dir) && != servers_dir` containment check on `target_dir` before the `remove_dir_all`/`create_dir_all`/extraction sequence (mirroring `uninstall_handler`'s bug-400 fix), and/or validate `entry.id`/`entry.directory` format at catalog-parse time. — FIXED 2026-07-13 (branch fix/audit-critical-high): vulnerable anchor removed; verify-issues [FIXED].

issues.summary: MEDIUM: Health-monitor auto-restart ignores a concurrent explicit stop/drain, silently reviving a server the operator just took down — `check_and_restart_dead_servers` takes an atomic snapshot of dead servers, then per-server does `tokio::time::sleep(backoff).await` followed by `manager.restart_server(&server_id).await` with no re-validation of the server's live status in between (the only in-loop recheck, at line 86, covers `setup_in_progress`, not the target server's own state). `restart_server` (mcp.rs) likewise never checks whether the handle was moved to `Disconnected`/`Draining` by a concurrent explicit `stop_server`/`drain_server` call before restarting.
