issues.summary: MEDIUM: cleanup_stale_callbacks never evicts callbacks that were never responded to, allowing unbounded growth of the MGP callback table — `EventManager::cleanup_stale_callbacks` (mcp_events.rs:266-274) uses `retain(|_, cb| !cb.responded || cb.created_at.elapsed() < timeout)`, which only removes callbacks that HAVE been responded to and have aged past the timeout; callbacks that are never responded to satisfy `!cb.responded == true` and are kept forever. Since `register_callback` has no cap and dedup only applies to exact-id repeats, any connected MCP server that keeps requesting callbacks without ever calling `mgp.callback.respond` causes the in-memory `callbacks` HashMap to grow without bound for the life of the kernel process — an unbounded-growth resource leak, in contrast to the capped `event_buffer` in the same file.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): events). Failure scenario: A connected MCP server (buggy or malicious) repeatedly issues `notifications/mgp.callback.request` with distinct `callback_id`s (e.g. via the `external_message`/confirm/generic callback types handled in `handle_callback_request`) and never receives a `mgp.callback.respond` for them. `register_callback` (mcp_events.rs:172-202) unconditionally inserts a new `PendingCallback` per unique id — the only dedup is on exact `callback_id` match, so a server can trivially avoid it by minting a new id each time. `cleanup_stale_callbacks`, the only pruning mechanism (invoked every health-check tick from managers/mcp_health.rs:44-46 with a 5-minute timeout), retains any entry where `!cb.responded` is true, i.e. it retains *every* unresponded callback regardless of age — only already-responded entries older than the timeout are ever removed. Unlike the sibling `event_buffer` (hard-capped at `MAX_BUFFER_SIZE = 1000`, mcp_events.rs:35/124-126), the `callbacks: Mutex<HashMap<String, PendingCallback>>` map has no size cap at all, so it grows without bound for the lifetime of the kernel process as unresponded callbacks (each carrying `message: String`, `options: Option<Vec<String>>`, and an unbounded `raw_metadata: Option<serde_json::Value>`) accumulate. Fix direction: Also age out unresponded callbacks past a (longer) TTL — e.g. resolve them with a synthetic timeout response and remove, or otherwise cap the map (a MAX_PENDING_CALLBACKS bound similar to MAX_BUFFER_SIZE) so a misbehaving or malicious server cannot grow kernel memory unboundedly by never responding.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: revoke_permission has a read-modify-write TOCTOU race that grant_permission was explicitly hardened against but revoke was not — revoke_permission's own comment says 'write back atomically' but the read (get_permissions) and the write (the UPDATE at line 188) are two separate, unsynchronized DB round-trips with no transaction or optimistic-concurrency guard — a classic lost-update race. This is the identical pattern that grant_permission (same file, ~line 203-227) was deliberately rewritten to fix via a single atomic SQL statement, per its own comment 'H-08: Single atomic SQL statement to prevent TOCTOU race in permission grant' — the fix was applied to grant but not to revoke, leaving the same class of bug live on the removal path.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): capabilities-consensus). Failure scenario: Two concurrent DELETE /api/plugins/:id/permissions requests target the same plugin_id but different permissions (e.g. revoke NetworkAccess and revoke FileWrite fired in parallel from two admin/dashboard sessions, or a bulk 'revoke all' UI action that fans out concurrent calls). Both calls execute get_permissions(plugin_id) (line 177) before either has written back, so both read the same starting allowed_permissions list. Call A computes the list with NetworkAccess removed and issues its UPDATE; call B — still working off its own stale pre-A snapshot — computes the list with only FileWrite removed (NetworkAccess still present) and its later UPDATE (line 188) overwrites A's write in full. The caller and audit log for call A both report NetworkAccess successfully revoked, and the in-memory effective_permissions retain-filter at line 197-198 also 'removes' it locally, yet the DB row (the source of truth on next load / for other readers) still has NetworkAccess granted — a silently lost revocation. Fix direction: Make the revoke path atomic the same way grant_permission was fixed: a single SQL UPDATE using json_remove (or an equivalent json_each/json_group_array filter) keyed only on plugin_id and the target permission, with no intervening application-level read-modify-write; or wrap get_permissions+UPDATE in a transaction with a WHERE clause guarding against concurrent modification of allowed_permissions.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: Cron scheduler silently swallows the post-dispatch DB update, letting a due job re-fire on the next tick — The success path in `tick()` sends the cron job's event and then tries to persist the new `next_run_at`/`enabled` state, but discards any error from that DB write with `.ok()` and never logs it. A transient DB failure (busy/lock timeout) therefore leaves the job's due-window state unchanged, causing it to be re-dispatched on the following tick — completely breaking the one-shot guarantee for `schedule_type="once"` jobs and enabling uncontrolled repeat dispatch for recurring ones, with zero observability into why.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): config-scheduler). Failure scenario: In `tick()`, after `event_tx.send(envelope).await` successfully dispatches a due job's message, the code computes `(next_run, still_enabled) = calculate_next_run(job, now_ms)` and calls `db::update_cron_job_run(...)` to persist `next_run_at`/`enabled` (this write is the ONLY mechanism that advances the job past its due window). The `.await.ok()` on line 199-200 discards any `Err` from that write with no logging at all. `update_cron_job_run` is wrapped in `db_timeout(...)` (see crates/core/src/db/cron.rs:86-95), so any transient SQLite contention/lock/timeout beyond `db_timeout_secs` returns Err. When that happens, the job's `next_run_at` in the DB is never advanced and (for `schedule_type="once"`) `enabled` stays `true`, so on the very next scheduler tick (every `cron_check_interval_secs`, minimum 10s) `db::get_due_cron_jobs` finds the SAME job still due and the kernel dispatches the SAME message again, spawning another full agentic-loop run. For a `once` job this breaks the explicit 'disable after execution' contract in `calculate_next_run` and can duplicate any side-effecting action the job performs (double API calls, double messages, etc.); for `interval`/`cron` jobs it produces uncontrolled re-dispatch until the DB write eventually succeeds — the exact 'perpetually due, re-dispatches a full agentic loop every tick' cost/availability DoS the file's own bug-405 comment (lines 16-22) warns about, just reached via a different (unlogged) path. Fix direction: Log the error (at minimum `error!`) instead of `.ok()`, and consider a bounded retry or marking the job for reconciliation on the next tick rather than leaving stale due-state; also add a test asserting a `once` job stays disabled/does not re-fire when the follow-up DB update fails.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: read_text_file is a capability-unscoped, unvalidated arbitrary-file-read command — `read_text_file` has no path allowlist/base-directory restriction and, unlike fs-plugin commands, isn't scoped by the capabilities ACL at all, so its safety today rests entirely on the frontend always routing it through a native file-picker — a convention rather than an enforced boundary.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): tauri-shell). Failure scenario: `read_text_file(path: String)` performs no validation of `path` and is registered as a plain #[tauri::command] (dashboard/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:597-611) with no corresponding entry in capabilities/default.json — Tauri v2's ACL governs plugin-namespaced permissions (core:*, shell:*, dialog:*, etc.) but app-defined commands registered via `tauri::generate_handler!` are invocable by any script running in the 'main' or 'vrm-viewer' webview regardless of the capabilities file. The only current caller (dashboard/src/components/settings/GeneralSection.tsx:84) gates `path` behind a native `openFileDialog()` picker, but that is a frontend convention, not a backend guarantee: any script able to execute `window.__TAURI__.core.invoke('read_text_file', {path: '/Users/victim/.ssh/id_rsa'})` in that webview (e.g. via a future XSS, given the CSP's script-src also allows 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval') reads any file the OS user can read and gets the contents back into JS. Fix direction: Either move file-import reads onto tauri-plugin-fs with an explicit `fs:scope` allowlist (gets ACL + scope enforcement for free), or add an explicit allow-list/base-dir check inside read_text_file so it can only serve paths under expected app directories (or paths just returned by the dialog plugin, tracked server-side).

issues.summary: MEDIUM: AgentTokenStream handler mutates pendingResponse without validating source_message_id, causing silent loss/corruption of a concurrent agent response — The AgentTokenStream SSE handler filters only on `agent_id === agent.id` and then unconditionally mutates the single per-console `pendingResponse` state, never checking `stream.source_message_id` against the response already in flight. Unlike the sibling ThoughtResponse handler (which finalizes any in-progress `prev` into `messages` before starting a new pendingResponse), this handler has no such finalization path, so an overlapping stream for a different source message either wholesale-replaces (dropping) or text-concatenates (corrupting) the response the user is actually waiting on.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): dash-agent-chat). Failure scenario: The same agent_id can be driven by multiple concurrent session_keys server-side (crates/core/src/managers/session_manager.rs SessionKey::new(agent_id, channel) — dashboard chat, cron dispatch, discord, etc. are independent sessions for the same agent, confirmed by run_agentic_loop having no per-agent mutual-exclusion lock). If a cron-triggered (or otherwise independently-triggered) agentic loop for this agent emits AgentTokenStream/ThoughtResponse events while the user's own exchange is mid-flight in this AgentConsole tab, two concrete corruptions occur: (1) if the user's own response already finished streaming and is a plain (non-streaming) pendingResponse mid-typewriter-animation, an unrelated AgentTokenStream chunk for a different source_message_id hits the `prev?.streaming` false branch and REPLACES pendingResponse wholesale with a brand-new streaming object — TypewriterMessage unmounts before firing onComplete, so the user's real response is never pushed into `messages` and is lost from the visible chat; (2) if the user's own response is itself still streaming, a chunk from the other loop is blindly appended via `prev.text + stream.delta` with no check that `stream.source_message_id` matches the message the current pendingResponse belongs to, silently interleaving two unrelated agent responses into one garbled text blob. Fix direction: Thread `source_message_id` (or the retry/parent id) through pendingResponse and compare it against `stream.source_message_id` before appending; if it doesn't match the currently displayed response, finalize the current pendingResponse into `messages` first (mirroring the ThoughtResponse handler's `if (prev) { ...push prevMsg...}` logic) before starting a new streaming entry for the unrelated message.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: Delete-agent password gate checks a metadata field the backend never sets, so the password prompt never appears and password-protected agent deletion always fails — AgentTerminal.tsx reads `agent.metadata?.has_password` to decide whether to show/require a password before deleting an agent, but the backend only ever populates `has_power_password` for this same underlying `power_password_hash` column (as used correctly elsewhere in PowerToggleModal.tsx and AgentConsole.tsx). The field-name drift means the password input is permanently hidden and every delete attempt on a protected agent is rejected server-side with no way to supply the password from the UI.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): dash-agent-chat). Failure scenario: For any agent that has a power password set, `power_password_hash IS NOT NULL` and the backend (crates/core/src/managers/agents.rs `row_to_metadata`) injects `has_power_password: "true"` into the returned metadata — it never injects a `has_password` key anywhere in the codebase (confirmed: `has_password` occurs nowhere in crates/*.rs, only ever read in this file). Because the delete-confirmation modal's password field, the disabled-state check, and `handleDeleteConfirm`'s `hasPassword` gate all key off the non-existent `metadata?.has_password`, the field is always falsy: the password `<input>` never renders, the Delete button is never disabled waiting for input, and `handleDeleteConfirm` always sends `password: undefined`. The backend's `verify_agent_password` (crates/core/src/handlers/utils.rs) correctly rejects the deletion with a `ValidationError('Password required to delete this agent')` — so there is no auth bypass — but the user is shown a generic failure with no way to enter the actual password, making it impossible to delete a password-protected agent through the dashboard UI at all. Fix direction: Change the three `deleteTarget.metadata?.has_password` checks (lines 242, 328, 353) to `deleteTarget.metadata?.has_power_password`, matching PowerToggleModal.tsx and AgentConsole.tsx.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: Lifecycle action button shows a false "success" checkmark after a failed start/stop/restart/delete, while the real error is hidden behind the modal — `handleAction` (lines 35-46) assumes `await fn()` not throwing means the action succeeded and unconditionally calls `setActionDone(action)`, but the `onStart`/`onStop`/`onRestart`/`onDelete` callbacks it receives are built from `useAsyncAction.run`, which swallows failures into an `error` state and always resolves. This produces a misleading local "done" (green check) UI state on failure, and the true error banner is rendered in the parent page behind the open modal, so no visible error indication reaches the user at all.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): dash-mcp-marketplace). Failure scenario: User opens a server's detail modal and clicks Stop/Start/Restart/Delete; the backend call fails (e.g. server busy, permission error, backend 500). `onStart`/`onStop`/`onRestart`/`onDelete` are all built in McpServersPage.tsx via `action.run(...)` from useAsyncAction, which catches the error internally, sets `action.error`, and resolves (never rejects) — see dashboard/src/hooks/useAsyncAction.ts lines 20-28 (`catch (err) { setError(...); return undefined; }`, no rethrow). Because `handleAction` in McpServerDetail.tsx has a try/finally with no catch and unconditionally runs `setActionDone(action)` right after `await fn()`, the button flips to a green CheckCircle "success" state even though the operation failed. Meanwhile the only error UI (`{action.error && <AlertCard>}`) lives in McpServersPage.tsx behind the modal's full-screen `Modal` backdrop (z-50 portal), so it is not visible while the detail modal is open. The user sees an affirmative success indicator and no error at all for a genuinely failed action. Fix direction: Have `handleAction` detect failure explicitly — e.g. have `onStart`/`onStop`/`onRestart`/`onDelete` return a success boolean (or rethrow) so `handleAction` can gate `setActionDone` on actual success, and/or surface `action.error` inside the modal (e.g. pass it down or lift the AlertCard into the Modal) so failures are visible while the modal is open.

issues.summary: MEDIUM: AudioPlaybackManager has no cancellation/sequencing across concurrent play() calls, causing overlapping stale audio and lipsync desync — `playBuffer()` has no per-call sequence token or AbortController; it only cancels a source that has ALREADY started playing (via `this.sourceNode`). A request still in flight (fetch/decode) at the time a newer request arrives is never invalidated, so an old, superseded speech request can finish decoding after a new one has already started, resulting in overlapping/garbled audio and mismatched visemes. This is directly reachable from normal SSE traffic handled in the in-scope VrmViewerPage.tsx, which itself does not await or serialize consecutive `avatar_speech_play` events.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): dash-vrm-avatar). Failure scenario: Two `avatar_speech_play` SSE events for the same agent arrive close together (e.g. two short TTS utterances in quick succession). VrmViewerPage's SSE handler (dashboard/src/vrm/VrmViewerPage.tsx, `avatar_speech_play` branch) calls `controllerRef.current?.playSpeechData(...)`/`playSpeech(...)` for each event without awaiting or cancelling the previous call. Inside `AudioPlaybackManager.playBuffer()`, `this.stop()` runs synchronously at entry, but if the prior call's `ctx.decodeAudioData()` hasn't resolved yet, `this.sourceNode` is still null so `stop()` is a no-op. When that prior decode later resolves, it creates and `.start()`s its own `AudioBufferSourceNode`, which now plays concurrently with the node from the newer call. Both nodes render to `ctx.destination` simultaneously, and whichever `playSpeech(Data)` promise resolves last calls `visemePlayer.playSync()` with its own timeline, desynchronizing lip-sync from the audio that is actually audible. Fix direction: Add a monotonically increasing generation/request counter (or AbortController) captured at the start of play()/playData()/playBuffer(); after each await, bail out without touching `this.sourceNode`/`_playing` if a newer request has since superseded it. Optionally abort the in-flight fetch when a new play() call arrives.

issues.summary: LOW: AllowedProcessCapability::execute allowlist-checks the command basename but executes the caller-supplied full path — The security check operates on Path::new(cmd).file_name() while the exec call operates on the raw cmd argument, so the allowlist can be defeated by supplying any path whose basename matches an allowed command name. Currently unreachable in production because the only call site (managers/plugin.rs:88) always constructs the capability with an empty allowlist (which short-circuits to deny-all at line 313), but the logic itself ships broken and would become exploitable the moment any code path configures a real allowlist for ProcessExecution.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): capabilities-consensus). Failure scenario: basename is derived from cmd via Path::file_name() (lines 308-311) and checked against allowed_commands (line 313), but the actual spawn at line 324 runs Command::new(cmd) — the original, unmodified caller-supplied string, not basename. If a deployment ever configures a non-empty allowlist (today the sole construction site, managers/plugin.rs:88, always passes an empty Vec, so every call is denied unconditionally before reaching this code), a caller could pass cmd = "/some/writable/dir/python3" where that path is an attacker-planted executable; basename resolves to the allowlisted "python3" and passes the check, but the process actually executed is the untrusted path, not a trusted system binary — a textbook allowlist-by-basename bypass. Fix direction: Either reject any cmd containing a path separator (only allow bare command names looked up via a fixed, trusted PATH), or resolve cmd against a trusted binary directory and execute the resolved path — never execute the raw untrusted cmd after having only validated its basename.

issues.summary: LOW: retry_response does not verify the fetched message belongs to the target agent, allowing cross-agent content injection — The retry endpoint fetches the original message solely by message_id and never checks `original.agent_id == agent_id` (the path parameter), so a caller can re-inject any message's content into a different agent's event stream by mismatching the path agent_id and message_id. This breaks the per-agent conversation isolation that get_messages/delete_messages otherwise enforce (both of those are agent_id-scoped queries), and skips the enabled-agent check that post_message performs.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): llm-proxy). Failure scenario: POST /api/chat/agent-B/messages/<message_id belonging to agent-A>/retry (any authenticated caller can pick an arbitrary agent_id/message_id pair). `db::get_chat_message_by_id` looks the message up purely by id (`SELECT ... FROM chat_messages WHERE id = ?`, db/chat.rs:203-213), with no filter on the path's agent_id. The handler then builds a fresh ClotoMessage whose `content` is agent-A's original text and whose `target_agent` is the path's agent-B, and dispatches it as a live MessageReceived event — agent-B ends up processing content that was only ever addressed to agent-A. Unlike post_message (which checks `get_agent_config`/`agent.enabled` for the path agent_id), retry_response performs no such check at all, so it can also target a disabled or nonexistent agent. Fix direction: After fetching `original`, verify `original.agent_id == agent_id` (404/400 otherwise), and add the same `agent.enabled` existence check that post_message performs before dispatching the retry event.

issues.summary: LOW: deny_permission and get_pending_permissions have zero test coverage, unlike the auth-gated approve_permission they mirror — permissions.rs implements three HTTP handlers with an identical shape (check_auth → DB mutation/read → ok_data); only approve_permission has integration test coverage for both its auth gate and success path. deny_permission (an authorization-gated, state-mutating endpoint that denies a pending permission request) and get_pending_permissions (a deliberately unauthenticated, data-disclosing read endpoint) have no test coverage at all, leaving the authorization-gate default-deny behavior for one of the two mutating permission endpoints completely unverified.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): test-coverage). Failure scenario: crates/core/tests/handlers_http_test.rs wires only the /api/permissions/{id}/approve route into its test router and has two tests for it (test_grant_permission_requires_auth verifying 403/401/400 without X-API-Key, and test_grant_permission_success verifying the happy path). The sibling /api/permissions/{id}/deny route (deny_permission, same check_auth(&state, &headers)? gate at line 104) and GET /api/permissions/pending (get_pending_permissions, intentionally unauthenticated per its own doc comment) are never registered in any test router and never invoked in any integration test across crates/core/tests/. If a future refactor accidentally dropped or reordered the check_auth call in deny_permission (the two handlers are adjacent and structurally near-identical to approve_permission, making a copy-paste regression plausible), or if get_pending_permissions' intentional no-auth behavior were flipped or exposed unexpected fields, no test would catch it — approve_permission's auth gate is locked in, deny_permission's is not. Fix direction: Register POST /api/permissions/{id}/deny and GET /api/permissions/pending in the handlers_http_test.rs router and add tests mirroring test_grant_permission_requires_auth / test_grant_permission_success for deny_permission, plus a test asserting get_pending_permissions returns data without an X-API-Key header (locking in its documented intentional behavior).

issues.summary: LOW: avatar_updated_at is dropped by update_agent_config's metadata-preservation CASE (incomplete fix vs. set_avatar) — Commit df55bb6 built the CASE-based preserve-list for avatar_path/avatar_description/vrm_path specifically so that the full-metadata-replace COALESCE pattern used by PUT /api/agents/:id would not clobber fields owned by the dedicated avatar/VRM APIs. Commit 39df825 (later) added a fourth field, avatar_updated_at, to set_avatar's json_set call and wired it into the frontend (dashboard/src/lib/agentIdentity.tsx) as the avatar cache-busting key, but never updated update_agent_config's preserve-list to include it. The doc comment at agents.rs:389-391 states the intent ('Preserve fields managed by dedicated APIs... Without this, COALESCE full-replacement would overwrite these fields') but the implementation is now incomplete relative to that stated contract — a regression introduced when the field set diverged from the preservation list. Impact is limited (the frontend falls back to a mount-time cache key when avatar_updated_at is absent, so the avatar still renders, just with a less stable cache-bust value), and clear_avatar similarly never removes avatar_updated_at on delete, compounding the drift.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): agents-session). Failure scenario: An agent has an avatar uploaded (set_avatar writes avatar_path, avatar_description, AND avatar_updated_at into metadata JSON, agents.rs line 258). The user then edits any other agent field via PUT /api/agents/:id (e.g. renames the agent or changes default_engine_id) without touching the avatar. update_agent_config's metadata-preserving CASE only re-injects avatar_path, avatar_description and vrm_path from the pre-update row (lines 397-410) — it never re-injects avatar_updated_at, so that key is silently dropped from metadata on every such update. Fix direction: Extend the CASE chain in update_agent_config to also re-inject '$.avatar_updated_at' from the pre-update metadata (mirroring the vrm_path/avatar_description/avatar_path pattern), and add its removal to clear_avatar's json_remove call for symmetry.

issues.summary: LOW: update_agent_config silently no-ops (returns Ok) for a non-existent agent_id — update_agent_config (crates/core/src/managers/agents.rs:380-425) runs `UPDATE agents SET ... WHERE id = ?5` and unconditionally returns Ok(()) without inspecting `rows_affected()`. Contrast with delete_agent in the same file (line 372: `if result.rows_affected() == 0 { return Err(...AgentNotFound...) }`), which correctly treats a 0-row UPDATE/DELETE as a 404-equivalent. The handler that calls update_agent_config (crates/core/src/handlers/agents.rs update_agent, lines 236-285) performs no upstream existence check either (unlike upload_avatar/upload_vrm, which call get_agent_config first as an explicit 'Verify agent exists' step). The net effect is that PUT /api/agents/:id is a silent no-op returning success for any nonexistent id, violating the 'silent no-ops that return success' correctness class and creating an inconsistent CRUD contract (Delete correctly 404s, Update does not).
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): agents-session). Failure scenario: Client calls PUT /api/agents/<id> where <id> does not exist (typo, stale UI state, or a race with a concurrent DELETE /api/agents/<id> from another tab/session). The UPDATE affects 0 rows, sqlx::execute() still returns Ok, update_agent_config returns Ok(()), and the handler responds 200 with {"data":{}} — the dashboard shows a successful save even though nothing was changed and the agent may not exist at all. Fix direction: Check `result.rows_affected() == 0` after the UPDATE in update_agent_config (as delete_agent already does) and return Err(cloto_shared::ClotoError::AgentNotFound(agent_id.to_string())) so the handler surfaces a proper 404/error instead of a fake 200 success.

issues.summary: LOW: Unchecked u64 addition when normalizing Anthropic-style token usage can overflow on untrusted MCP-server output — `normalize_usage`'s fallback `total_tokens = prompt + completion` uses a raw, unchecked `u64` addition on values sourced directly from an untrusted MCP mind-server JSON response, so a hostile or buggy provider can trigger an overflow panic (debug builds) or a silently wrapped, corrupted token count (release builds) that then gets surfaced to the dashboard.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): config-scheduler). Failure scenario: `normalize_usage` is fed the `usage` JSON block returned inside a mind MCP server's `think()`/`think_with_tools()` response text (crates/core/src/handlers/system.rs:3062-3066, `maybe_record_usage`). For Anthropic-shaped responses (`{input_tokens, output_tokens}`, no `total_tokens` field — this is the documented, common case per the doc comment), `total` is computed as `prompt + completion`, both `u64` values taken directly from the provider's JSON via `as_u64()` with no upper-bound check. A malicious or malfunctioning provider/MCP server (these are user-pluggable, including third-party/self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints) can supply `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens` close to `u64::MAX`, causing this addition to overflow: in a debug build this panics (`attempt to add with overflow`), and in a release build (default Cargo profile, no `overflow-checks`) it silently wraps to an incorrect small value that is then stored via `UsageStore::record` and surfaced to the dashboard as the agent's 'used / max' token usage, corrupting the displayed accounting. Fix direction: Use `prompt.saturating_add(completion)` (or `checked_add` with a fallback) instead of the raw `+`, matching the saturating style already used a few lines below for the `u32::try_from(...).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)` clamps.

issues.summary: LOW: capture_screen exposes silent, unconfirmed full-screen capture with no current caller and no ACL scoping — An unused, privacy-sensitive command (silent screen capture) is exposed on the IPC surface with no gating and no current consumer, widening the attack surface beyond what the shipped app actually needs — a violation of least-privilege command exposure.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): tauri-shell). Failure scenario: `capture_screen` is registered in `invoke_handler` (line ~599) and captures the primary monitor to a base64 PNG with zero consent prompt, rate limit, or capability gating; it is not called anywhere in dashboard/src (confirmed via repo-wide search — no `captureScreen`/`capture_screen` call site exists in the frontend). Because it, like the other custom commands, is not represented in capabilities/default.json, any script with IPC access in the 'main' or 'vrm-viewer' webview can invoke it directly today and silently exfiltrate a screenshot of the user's desktop back into the webview, with no legitimate current feature relying on it. Fix direction: Remove capture_screen from invoke_handler until a concrete feature needs it, or gate it behind an explicit user-consent flow and a capability permission scoped to the specific window/feature that uses it.

issues.summary: LOW: Avatar cache-busting key setter is never called, so the cache-buster is a permanent no-op constant — The avatar cache-busting mechanism (`avatarKey` query param) is dead code: its setter is unused, so the value never changes and the intended per-upload cache invalidation never happens, risking a stale avatar being displayed after replacement.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): dash-agent-chat). Failure scenario: AvatarSection.tsx builds the persisted-avatar display URL as `${api.getAvatarUrl(agent.id)}?v=${avatarKey}` specifically to bust the browser HTTP cache after an avatar is replaced. Because `_setAvatarKey` is never invoked anywhere in the codebase, `avatarKey` is always `0`, so the query string is always `?v=0` across every avatar upload. After `handleAvatarUpload` → Save → a later re-open of this workspace (a fresh mount, so the local blob `avatarPreviewUrl` is gone and the UI falls back to the persisted-URL branch), the browser may serve a stale cached image from a previous `?v=0` fetch instead of the newly-uploaded one. Fix direction: Increment `avatarKey` (call the setter, dropping the underscore-prefixed unused naming) whenever a new avatar is successfully uploaded/saved, or derive the cache-buster from the upload timestamp/avatar_path instead of an untouched local counter.

issues.summary: LOW: Server-log history seeding can duplicate lines that already streamed in live via SSE — The history-seed effect merges fetched history (`seeded`) with whatever has already arrived live (`prev`) via straight concatenation (`[...seeded, ...prev]`) whenever `prev.length !== 0`, with no de-duplication. Because the ring-buffer history snapshot and the live SSE tail can overlap for events emitted right around mount time, the same log line can appear twice in the rendered list until it ages out of the 200-line cap.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): dash-mcp-marketplace). Failure scenario: User opens the Logs tab for a server that is actively emitting log lines. `useEventStream` starts appending live entries to `logs` immediately on mount (line 100-106), while the separate `getHistory()` fetch (lines 115-134) resolves asynchronously afterward. Any log event that both (a) is included in the kernel's event-history ring buffer snapshot returned by `getHistory()` and (b) has already arrived live via SSE before that fetch resolves ends up counted twice: once in `prev` (from the live listener) and once in `seeded` (from history), because the merge at line 126 unconditionally prepends `seeded` to `prev` with no de-duplication key. Fix direction: De-duplicate on merge, e.g. key entries by a stable id (timestamp+label+message, or an event sequence number from the backend) and filter `seeded` down to entries not already present in `prev` before concatenating.

issues.summary: LOW: detectPreset mutates the shared, exported preset server-id constants in place via Array.prototype.sort() — `detectPreset` is used as a read-only 'what preset is this?' query but has the side effect of mutating shared, exported module-level constants via in-place `.sort()`, because `preset.servers` aliases the original arrays rather than a defensive copy. Currently no consumer (`SetupWizard.tsx`, `ServerAccessSection.tsx`) depends on the original declared order — all usages convert the array to a `Set` or only read `.length` — so there is no presently-visible breakage, but this is a genuine, reachable mutation of state that callers reasonably assume is immutable and read-only.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): dash-services-state). Failure scenario: `SERVER_PRESETS[i].servers` is not a copy — it directly references the exported `STANDARD_SERVERS` / `ADVANCED_SERVERS` / `EXPERT_SERVERS` / `MINIMAL_SERVERS` arrays (e.g. `{ id: 'advanced', ..., servers: ADVANCED_SERVERS }`). `ServerAccessSection.tsx` calls `detectPreset(grantedIds, grantedServers)` unconditionally on every render (`const activePreset = detectPreset(...)` in the component body). `Array.prototype.sort()` sorts in place and returns the same reference, so the very first render of that component permanently reorders these exported constants for the remainder of the page session — any other module that imports `STANDARD_SERVERS`/`ADVANCED_SERVERS`/etc. and relies on their declared (curated) order will silently see alphabetical order instead from that point on. Fix direction: Sort a copy instead of the original array, e.g. `[...preset.servers].sort().join(',')`, and likewise `[...nonEngine].sort()` for symmetry/clarity even though `nonEngine` is already a fresh array.

issues.summary: LOW: openVrmWindow toggle has an unguarded check-then-act race that can desync tracked window state from the real OS window — `openVrmWindow` implements an open/close toggle using module-level mutable state (`vrmWindowOpen`, `vrmWindowRef`) that is read, then (after an `await import(...)` yield point) written, with no mutex/in-flight guard and no caller-side debouncing. Two overlapping invocations can both see the pre-toggle state and both take the 'create a new window' branch, producing a duplicate-label window-construction race and a state/reality desync for the toggle.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): dash-services-state). Failure scenario: In AgentConsole.tsx the VRM toggle button calls `onClick={() => openVrmWindow(agent.id, api.apiKey)}` with no disabling/debouncing while the async call is in flight. `openVrmWindow` first `await`s a dynamic import (`@tauri-apps/api/webviewWindow`) before reading/writing the module-level `vrmWindowOpen`/`vrmWindowRef` flags. If the user double-clicks quickly (very plausible on the very first click, when that chunk import has not been cached/parsed yet), both invocations observe `vrmWindowOpen === false` before either sets it to `true`, so both proceed past the 'toggle off' and 'getByLabel' branches and both call `new WebviewWindow('vrm-viewer', {...})`. Tauri window labels must be unique; the second construction either errors (caught, and the catch handler resets `vrmWindowOpen=false; vrmWindowRef=null` even though the first call's window is genuinely open on screen) or otherwise leaves the two async calls fighting over the same module-level refs. Net effect: the tracked state (`vrmWindowOpen`/`vrmWindowRef`) can end up out of sync with reality — a window is visibly open but the toggle believes it is closed, so the next click tries to 'open' again instead of closing it. Fix direction: Add an in-flight guard (e.g. a module-level `Promise` or boolean lock that subsequent calls await/no-op against) around the whole toggle body, or disable the calling button while the promise is pending; alternatively always resolve state from `WebviewWindow.getByLabel()` results rather than trusting a check performed before the async gap.

issues.summary: LOW: VrmContext's agentState reset effect has an empty dependency array, contradicting its own "reset on vrmEnabled change" intent — The comment documents intent to reset `agentState` whenever `vrmEnabled` changes, but the effect's dependency array is `[]` (mount-only), so it can never respond to `vrmEnabled` changes as written. Verified via repo-wide grep that `VrmProvider`/`useVrmContext` currently have zero importers anywhere under dashboard/src, so this exact code path cannot execute today, but the defect is real and will activate the moment this context is wired into any agent-switching UI.
issues.pattern: Reset state when vrmEnabled changes \(agent switch\)
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): dash-vrm-avatar). Failure scenario: If `VrmProvider` were mounted around a component whose `vrmEnabled` prop toggles across an agent switch (as the comment explicitly describes), `agentState` would never reset to 'idle' on that transition, because the `useEffect` on lines 39-41 has dependency array `[]` and therefore only fires once on initial mount. A stale 'thinking'/'responding' state from the previous agent would carry over into the newly selected agent's avatar rendering. Fix direction: Change the dependency array to `[vrmEnabled]`, or remove/correct the misleading comment if mount-only reset is actually intended.

issues.summary: LOW: VrmaLoader.stop()'s uncancelled setTimeout can clobber a later playAnimation() call — `stop()`'s deferred cleanup path is timer-driven and never cancelled/cleared by a subsequent `playAnimation()` or `stop()` call, unlike the frame-driven (and correctly interruptible) pose-mode branch in `update()`. This is a missed-timer-cancellation bug. Currently `playAnimation()`/`loadVrmaAnimationFile()` has zero callers anywhere in dashboard/src — only the pose-mode path (`loadVrmaPoseFile`, wired to VrmViewerPage's drag-and-drop UI) is reachable, and that path is unaffected since its stop/fade logic runs entirely inside the per-frame `update()` rather than via `setTimeout`.
issues.notes: Discovered by ClotoCore comprehensive code-quality audit 2026-07-12 (an earlier decision / an earlier decision; Sonnet-5 Workflow wf_3a2b40c2-649 resume: 26 finders -> dedup 63 -> severity-tiered adversarial verify (all 160 agents, 0 error); final verdict CONFIRMED; finder(s): dash-vrm-avatar). Failure scenario: In animation-mixer mode (reached only via the public `VrmAnimationController.loadVrmaAnimationFile()` → `VrmaLoader.playAnimation()`), calling `stop(transitionSec)` schedules a bare `setTimeout` that force-stops the mixer and clears `currentAction`/`_active` after `transitionSec*1000` ms, without storing the timer handle. If `playAnimation()` starts a new animation before that timeout elapses, the stale timer still fires afterward, calling `mixer.stopAllAction()` and nulling `currentAction`/`_active` — silently killing the animation that was started in the interim, with no error surfaced to the caller. Fix direction: Store the setTimeout id (e.g. `this.stopTimeoutId = setTimeout(...)`) and clear any pending one at the top of `stop()`/`playAnimation()`; or drive the mixer-mode fade-out/stop through the existing per-frame `update()` the same way the pose-mode branch already does, eliminating the wall-clock timer entirely.
